Le projet combine des données multisources sur le trafic, l'infrastructure, les véhicules et la santé avec l'expérimentation immersive eXtended Reality (XR) et l'intelligence artificielle explicable pour analyser des situations critiques en matière de sécurité qui sont rares, sous-déclarées ou impossibles à observer sur le plan éthique dans le trafic réel. L'IA explicable assure la transparence et l'interprétation, appuyant la confiance, la transférabilité et la pertinence des politiques. Le projet traduit ces informations en méthodes d'évaluation harmonisées, en modèles de prévision et en indicateurs validés, permettant une évaluation et une comparaison solides des interventions réglementaires, infrastructurelles, technologiques et comportementales des parties prenantes à l'approche du système sûr. Une attention particulière est accordée aux interactions entre les utilisateurs avec des masses et des vitesses différentes, y compris les vélos électroniques, les vélos e-cargo et les e-cooters, pour la mobilité personnelle et la logistique urbaine. Des projets pilotes de grande envergure dans quatre villes européennes valident des méthodes de trafic réel, soutiennent l'apprentissage interurbain et garantissent leur applicabilité dans des conditions de sécurité, d'infrastructure et de culture diverses. Mis en œuvre par un consortium multidisciplinaire d'ingénierie, de science comportementale, de XR, d'IA, d'urbanisme et de politique, le projet fournit des orientations concrètes et standardisées qui accélèrent des systèmes actifs plus sûrs, plus inclusifs et de micromobilité dans toute l'Europe. La planification de systèmes de transport urbain sûrs est intrinsèquement complexe : les interventions durent des décennies, nécessitent des investissements importants, doivent s'adapter à des espaces restreints et doivent répondre à des besoins changeants des utilisateurs. Les méthodes modernes de collecte de données - telles que les capteurs de véhicules embarqués à haute fréquence et les images de vision par ordinateur - sont bien adaptées pour saisir ces complexités grâce à des aperçus à haute résolution en temps quasi réel. Cependant, la collecte, le traitement et l'opérationnalisation de ces volumes de mégadonnées sont un défi en raison de structures de données hétérogènes et de fortes demandes de calcul. Description de l'emploi Ce doctorat vise à faire progresser l'état de la technique en matière de fusion des données de détection et de télédétection pour l'analyse de la sécurité des infrastructures de transport urbain. Le candidat développera de nouveaux outils et méthodes qui intègrent les mégadonnées, la vision informatique et l'apprentissage automatique. Les principales tâches du candidat seront les suivantes : • Développer un pipeline de détection évolutive : concevoir et mettre en œuvre une architecture logicielle/outil capable de traiter des flux de données multisources de capteurs, de caméras et de télédétection de véhicules • Automatiser l'identification des caractéristiques et des facteurs: Train machine learning et les modèles de vision informatique dans le pipeline pour détecter automatiquement les caractéristiques de l'infrastructure bâtie et les facteurs connexes affectant la sécurité et le confort de la micromobilité • Générer la cartographie et les sorties diagnostiques : s'assurer que le logiciel accepte divers intrants et génère des sorties de données structurées et de haute qualité optimisées pour la cartographie spatiale, le diagnostic des risques et la modélisation de la sécurité prédictive en aval • Collaborer via Real-World Pilots: Valider et affiner le pipeline à l'aide de données réelles provenant des villes pilotes du projet, en travaillant en coope proche

Sind Sie bereit, Ihre Expertise im Projektmanagement in spannenden Projekten einzusetzen und innovative Lösungen umzusetzen? Werden Sie Teil unseres Teams und übernehmen Sie eine wichtige Rolle in der Gestaltung und Umsetzung von Bauprojekten an der ETH Zürich!

Sie arbeiten eng mit unseren Fachabteilungen Engineering & Systeme sowie Facility Services zusammen.

Zudem steuern Sie Projektteams, die aus internen und externen Fachleuten bestehen, koordinieren die verschiedenen Stakeholder wie Behörden sowie Nutzende und gewährleisten die Einhaltung von Kosten, Terminen und Qualitätsstandards.

Ihre Projekte setzen Sie meist mit Einzelleistungsträgermodellen oder Generalplaner um, bringen aber auch alternative Ansätze nach Design-Build gewinnbringend ein.

• Technische Ausbildung: Sie haben einen Hochschulabschluss in Architektur, Bauingenieurwesen oder einem ähnlichen Fach und verfügen über ausgewiesenes Fachwissen im Projektmanagement und/oder Baumanagement.

• Projekterfahrung: Dank Ihrer mehrjährigen Erfahrung als Projektleiter für Umbauten oder Sanierungen komplexer Bauvorhaben sind Sie mit der Koordination von Fachteams in allen SIA-Phasen vertraut. Interdisziplinäre Aufgaben bereiten Ihnen Freude.

• Starke Kommunikation: Sie bauen schnell konstruktive Beziehungen auf, schaffen Vertrauen und gestalten Ihre Zusammenarbeit effektiv und zielführend.

Freuen Sie sich auf eine vielseitige Tätigkeit mit Gestaltungsfreiraum und Verantwortung in einem dynamischen, forschungsnahen Umfeld. «MACHEN – menschlich, gemeinsam, nachhaltig».

Entrate a far parte del nostro team e giocate un ruolo importante nella progettazione e realizzazione di progetti di costruzione a Zurigo! jobs.description:
Doktorand:in in Rechtswissenschaften (m/w/d)

100%, Zürich, befristet

print
Drucken

Im Rahmen des SNF-geförderten Projekts „Responsible AI for the Swiss Judiciary" untersuchen wir gemeinsam mit Schweizer Gerichten, wie künstliche Intelligenz verantwortungsvoll in die Justiz integriert werden kann.

Projekthintergrund

Die Doktorandenstelle ist auf die empirische Erforschung von KI-gestützten Entscheidungshilfen in der Justiz ausgerichtet. Die doktorierende Person wird die Auswirkungen solcher Systeme auf die richterliche Praxis untersuchen – durch die Konzeption und Durchführung von Feldexperimenten in Zusammenarbeit mit Schweizer Gerichten sowie deren rechtliche und institutionelle Evaluation.

Stellenbeschreibung

• Untersuchung richterlicher Entscheidungsprozesse und juristischer Argumentation im Zusammenspiel mit KI-Tools

• Mitwirkung bei der Entwicklung von Experimentdesigns und Evaluierungsrahmen für KI-gestützte Entscheidungsfindung

• Zusammenarbeit mit dem technischen Team zur Erforschung der Interaktion zwischen KI-Systemen und juristischen Nutzern

• Publikation von Forschungsergebnissen in führenden Fachzeitschriften und Präsentation auf internationalen Konferenzen

• Die Stelle ist als kumulative Dissertation an der Schnittstelle von Rechtswissenschaft, Informatik und empirischer Sozialwissenschaft konzipiert

• Unsere Büros befinden sich in der Zürcher Innenstadt

• Die Arbeitssprachen sind Deutsch und Englisch

Profil

• Einen hervorragenden Bachelor- und Masterabschluss in Rechtswissenschaften von einer deutschsprachigen Universität (Deutschland, Österreich oder Schweiz) mitbringen

• Ein ausgeprägtes Interesse an den Auswirkungen von KI auf Recht und Gesellschaft haben

• Interesse an Feldexperimenten und experimentellen Forschungsdesigns mitbringen

• Die Bereitschaft zeigen, quantitative und empirische Forschungsmethoden zu erlernen und anzuwenden

• Über sehr gute Englischkenntnisse verfügen; Deutsch- und Französischkenntnisse sind von Vorteil

Arbeitsort

Arbeitsort

Wir bieten

• Ihr Beruf mit Wirkung: Werden Sie Teil der ETH Zürich, die nicht nur Ihre berufliche Entwicklung unterstützt, sondern auch aktiv zu positiven Veränderungen in der Gesellschaft beiträgt

• Es erwarten Sie zahlreiche Vergünstigungen , wie z.B. ÖV-Abonnemente und Car Sharing, ein breites Sportangebot des ASVZ , Kinderbetreuung sowie attraktive Vorsorgeleistungen

chevron_right
Arbeiten, Lehren und Forschen an der ETH Zürich

Diversität und Nachhaltigkeit sind uns wichtig

Im Einklang mit unseren Werten unterstützt die ETH Zürich eine inklusive Kultur. Wir fördern Chancengleichheit, schätzen Vielfalt und pflegen ein Arbeits- und Lernumfeld, in dem die Rechte und die Würde aller Mitarbeitenden und Studierenden respektiert werden. Auf unserer Webseite zur Chancengleichheit und Vielfalt erfahren Sie, wie wir ein faires und offenes Umfeld sicherstellen, in dem sich alle entwickeln und entfalten können. Nachhaltigkeit ist für uns ein zentraler Wert – wir arbeiten konsequent an einer klimaneutralen Zukunft.

Neugierig? Sind wir auch.

Wir freuen uns auf Ihre Online-Bewerbung mit den folgenden Unterlagen:

• Motivationsschreiben (mit Angaben zu Ihrer relevanten Erfahrung für das genannte Projekt sowie Ihrer Motivation)

• Lebenslauf

• Zeugnisse und Notenausweise

Weitere Informationen über Center for Law & Economics sowie zum SNF-Projekt , finden Sie auf den folgenden Webseiten: Center for Law & Economics und SNF-Projekt . Für Auskünfte steht Ihnen Dr. Jakob Merane, (jmerane@ethz.ch) (keine Bewerbungsunterlagen), gerne zur Verfügung.

Die Doktorandenstelle ist an der Professur von Prof. Alexander Stremitzer angesiedelt.

Bitte bewerben Sie sich ausschliesslich über das Online-Bewerbungsportal. Bewerbungen per E-Mail sowie auf dem Postweg werden nicht berücksichtigt.

&Uuml

Promuoviamo pari opportunità, apprezziamo la diversità e promuoviamo un ambiente di lavoro e di apprendimento in cui vengono rispettati i diritti e la dignità di tutti i dipendenti e gli studenti. Sul nostro sito web su pari opportunità e diversità, imparerai come garantire un ambiente equo e aperto in cui tutti possono sviluppare e sviluppare. La sostenibilità è un valore centrale per noi – lavoriamo costantemente su un futuro neutro dal clima. --- Contatto Curioso? Anche noi. Per informazioni si prega di contattare il Dr. Jakob Merane (jmerane@ethz.ch) (nessun documento di richiesta). La posizione di dottorato è alla cattedra del Prof. Alexander Stremitzer si stabilì. Si prega di applicare esclusivamente tramite il portale di applicazione online. Le domande via e-mail e per posta non sono prese in considerazione.
descriptionByLocale.en: Dottorando/a in Giurisprudenza 100%, Zurigo, a tempo determinato --- descrizione As part of the SNSF-funded project „Responsible AI for the Swiss Judiciary, we are working together with Swiss courts to investigate how artificial intelligence can be responsibly integrated into justice. Project background The PhD student body is responsible for the empirical research of AI-based decision-making aids in the judiciary. The doctoral student will investigate the effects of such systems on judicial practice – through the design and implementation of field experiments in cooperation with Swiss courts and their legal and institutional evaluation. --- Mansioni - Investigation of judicial decision-making processes and legal argumentation in interaction with AI tools - Participation in the development of experimental design and evaluation frameworks for AI-based decision-making - Cooperation with the technical team to investigate the interaction between AI systems and legal users - Publication of research results in leading journals and presentation at international conferences - The body is conceived as a cumulative dissertation at the interface of law, computer science and empirical social science - Our offices are located in Zurich city centre - The working languages are German and English. --- • Requisiti - Bring an excellent Bachelor and Master's degree in Law from a German-speaking university (Germany, Austria or Switzerland) - A strong interest in the impact of AI on law and society - Bringing interest in field experiments and experimental research designs - The willingness to learn and apply quantitative and empirical research methods - have very good English skills; German and French skills are advantageous --- Luogo di lavoro --- • Cosa offriamo - Your profession with effect: Be part of ETH Zurich, which not only supports your professional development, but also actively contributes to positive changes in society - There are numerous benefits, such as ÖV subscriptions and Car Sharing, a wide range of sports activities at ASVZ, childcare and attractive pensions. --- Diversità e sostenibilità In line with our values, ETH Zurich supports an inclusive culture. We promote equal opportunities, appreciate diversity and foster a working and learning environment in which the rights and dignity of all employees and students are respected. On our website on equal opportunities and diversity, you will learn how to ensure a fair and open environment in which everyone can develop and develop. Sustainability is a central value for us – we work consistently on a climate-neutral future. --- Contatto Curious? So are we. We look forward to your online application with the following documents: - Letter of motivation (with information on your relevant experience for the project and your motivation) - CV - Certificates and certificates For more information about Center for Law & Economics and the SNSF project, see the following websites: Center for Law & Economics and SNSF project. For information please contact Dr. Jakob Merane (jmerane@ethz.ch) (no application documents). The doctoral position is at the professorship of Prof. Alexander Stremitzer settled. Please apply exclusively via the online application portal. Applications by e-mail and by post are not taken into account.

jobs.description:
PhD Position in Computer Vision Applied to Natural Hazards

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

The Engineering Geology group at ETH Zurich (Prof. Jordan Aaron) is seeking a motivated and creative doctoral student who specializes in computer vision. The position can commence as early as September 1st, 2026 (negotiable), and is fully funded for four years.

Job description

• Improving our understanding of the mechanisms that govern debris flow motion is a core research topic in the Chair of Engineering Geology at ETHZ

• As part of this, the group collects and analyses an unprecendented set of field datasets

• The collected data includes timelapse point clouds, video imagery, as well as auxilary data including environmental parameter timeseries

• This data is then processed to derive high temporal and spatial resolution estimates of displacement, velocity, strain and surface change, as well as the driving mechanisms

• A large foundational dataset has already been collected, and presents a unique opportunity for making new insights into debris-flow processes

• You will develop advanced algorithms to process this data, with a focus on optical flow and object detection

• You will interpret the results to better understand debris flow mechanisms

• You will also contribute to the maintenance and upkeep of the monitoring systems

• Additionally, you will be given signficiant support to develop your own research ideas and apply for third party funding

• Contributions to teaching within the Engineering Geology group are also expected

Profile

• Masters degree in Computer Vision, Data Science, Computer Science, Mechatronics, Remote Sensing, Engineering Geology or other related discipline

• Demonstrated expertise and interest in machine learning and computer vision algorithms is necessary, with an emphasis on object tracking, optical flow and sensor fusion

• Knowledge of rock mechanics, soil mechanics and/or landslide processes is considered beneficial

• Prior experience with point cloud processing is an asset

• Ability to work independently

• Strong written and oral communication skills in English

Workplace

Workplace

We offer

• We are an enthusiastic and collaborative research group with many opportunities for multi-disciplinary cutting edge research in engineering geology

• There are significant opportunities to broaden your research interests, and develop your academic career

• Your job with impact: Become part of ETH Zurich, which not only supports your professional development, but also actively contributes to positive change in society

• You can expect numerous benefits , such as public transport season tickets and car sharing, a wide range of sports offered by the ASVZ , childcare and attractive pension benefits

chevron_right
Working, teaching and research at ETH Zurich

We value diversity and sustainability

In line with our values , ETH Zurich encourages an inclusive culture. We promote equality of opportunity, value diversity and nurture a working and learning environment in which the rights and dignity of all our staff and students are respected. Visit our Equal Opportunities and Diversity website to find out how we ensure a fair and open environment that allows everyone to grow and flourish. Sustainability is a core value for us – we are consistently working towards a climate-neutral future .

Curious? So are we.

We look forward to receiving your online application until 1 July 2026 with the following documents:

• Brief cover letter summarizing your motivation for applying for the position

• Your academic CV

• Contact details of two references (no need for reference letters)

• Transcripts

Further information about the Gelogical Institute can be found on our Website . Questions regarding the position should be directed to Prof. Jordan Aaron, jordan.aaron@eaps.ethz.ch (no applications).

Please note that we exclusively accept applications submitted through our online application portal. Applicat

Jordan Aaron) cherche un doctorant motivé et créatif qui se spécialise dans la vision informatique. Le poste peut commencer dès le 1er septembre 2026 (négociable) et est entièrement financé pendant quatre ans. Description du poste • Améliorer notre compréhension des mécanismes qui régissent le mouvement de l'écoulement des débris est un thème de recherche essentiel de la chaire d'ingénierie géologique à ETHZ • Dans ce cadre, le groupe recueille et analyse un ensemble de données de terrain non précendentes • Les données collectées comprennent les nuages ponctuels, les images vidéo, ainsi que les données auxiliaires, y compris les séries chronologiques des paramètres environnementaux • Ces données sont ensuite traitées pour obtenir des estimations de haute résolution temporelle et spatiale du déplacement, de la vitesse, de la déformation et du changement de surface, ainsi que des mécanismes de conduite • Un vaste ensemble de données fondamentales a déjà été collecté et offre une occasion unique de faire de nouveaux éclairages sur les processus d'écoulement des débris. • Vous développerez des algorithmes avancés pour traiter ces données, en mettant l'accent sur le flux optique et la détection d'objets • Vous interpréterez les résultats pour mieux comprendre les mécanismes d'écoulement des débris • Vous contribuerez également à l'entretien et à l'entretien des systèmes de surveillance • En outre, vous bénéficierez d'un soutien significatif pour développer vos propres idées de recherche et faire une demande de financement par des tiers • Des contributions à l'enseignement au sein du groupe d'ingénierie géologique sont également attendues Profil • Maîtrise en informatique, informatique, mécatronique, télédétection, géologie ou autre discipline connexe • Une expertise démontrée et un intérêt pour l'apprentissage automatique et les algorithmes de vision par ordinateur sont nécessaires, en mettant l'accent sur le suivi des objets, le flux optique et la fusion des capteurs • La connaissance de la mécanique des roches, de la mécanique des sols et/ou des processus de glissement de terrain est considérée comme bénéfique • L'expérience préalable avec le traitement point cloud est un atout • Capacité de travailler de manière indépendante • Fortes compétences en communication écrite et orale en anglais Lieu de travail Nous offrons • Nous sommes un groupe de recherche enthousiaste et collaboratif qui offre de nombreuses possibilités de recherche multidisciplinaire de pointe en géologie de l'ingénierie • Il y a d'importantes possibilités d'élargir vos intérêts de recherche et de développer votre carrière universitaire • Votre travail avec impact: Devenez membre de l'ETH Zurich, qui non seulement soutient votre développement professionnel, mais contribue également activement au changement positif dans la société • Vous pouvez vous attendre à de nombreux avantages , tels que les billets de saison de transport public et le partage de voiture , un large éventail de sports offerts par l'ASVZ , garde d'enfants et prestations de retraite attrayantes chevron droit Travail, enseignement et recherche à l'ETH Zurich Nous PhD Position in Numerical Modelling of Debris Flows

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

The Chair of Engineering Geology (Prof. Dr. Jordan Aaron, Geological Institute) is looking for a creative and motivated PhD candidate with a strong interest in fluid mechanics and numerical modelling. The position is expected to start in September 2026 and is fully funded for 4 years.

Job description

• You will develop a new coupled solid/ fluid mechanics-based numerical model to simulate the motion of debris flows

• You will incorporate novel field data currently being collected at numerous locations around the world to validate the new numerical model

• You will combine the numerical model results with field data to further our understanding of the motion of debris flows

Profile

• MSc in Fluid Mechanics, Hydraulics, Engineering Geology, Geological Engineering, Geophysics or related fields

• Strong background in numerical modelling

• Interest in natural hazards

• Motivation, creativity, independence, and ability to work in a team

• Excellent English communication skills

jobs.description:
Systems Engineer – Platform Automation

80%-100%, Lugano, fixed-term

print
Drucken

The Swiss National Supercomputing Centre (CSCS) develops and operates a high-performance computing and data research infrastructure that supports world-class science in Switzerland. Its user laboratory is available to domestic and international researchers in academia, industry, and the business sector. The centre is operated by ETH Zurich and has offices at its data centre in Lugano and in Zurich.

For this position the work location is Lugano.

Project background

As high-performance computing, AI, and cloud technologies continue to converge; CSCS is redefining how advanced computational services are designed and delivered. Modern scientific and engineering workloads are no longer just large—they are complex, data-intensive, and highly diverse, pushing existing infrastructure to its limits.

We are offering a contract initially limited to two years , which will provide the opportunity to contribute to a fast-evolving AI landscape in which CSCS plays a key role and to support high-impact initiatives both nationally and internationally. This includes contributions to the Swiss AI Initiative and similar programs, such as lending support for the development and release of foundation models in the weather and climate domain.

The initial two-year contract could potentially be extended or even become permanent.

Job description

The main goal of this position is to develop and manage HPC/AI services on top of a multi-tenant infrastructure. As a Platform automation engineer, you will directly contribute to the design, implementation, maintenance, and documentation of platform services to support HPC and AI. Your work will directly enhance the overall system functionality and efficiency.

Main duties:

• Investigating, troubleshooting, and debugging platform services and infrastructure resources

• Developing, maintaining, and supporting tools and pipelines to support platforms on a geographically redundant infrastructure

• Developing automations to provision, test, deploy, and monitor resources to support the needs of HPC and AI platforms

• Supporting, documenting, and sharing knowledge of tools, and procedur

Profile

You should have a bachelor’s or higher degree in computer engineering, computer science, a relevant technical field, or equivalent practical experience.

You should have a sound knowledge of: 

• Experience in the deployment of HPC, AI, or Cloud infrastructures

• Management of HPC/AI services to maximize utilization of compute, storage and high speed network components

• Working knowledge of automation tools and frameworks, including CI/CD processes and ecosystem

• Linux administration skills

Experience with the following is preferred, though there will be ample opportunities to learn and gain more experience with all of these skills on the job:

• Versioning systems and CI/CD workflows such as ArgoCD

• Debugging of microservices running on Kubernetes

• Performance monitoring and diagnostic tools for HPC/AI hardware

• Infrastructure as Code tools such as Terraform and Ansible

Personal qualities:

• Self-motivated and proactive team player

• Strong communication skills or interest in developing them

• Strong problem-solving mindset with tolerance for uncertainty and change

• Understands user needs and works collaboratively to address them

• Adaptive and willing to learn new technologies with and from others

• Comfortable tackling complex or ambiguous problems

• Comfortable admitting when you don’t know, reaching out and leveraging the right expertise when needed

Project management and methodology:

• Experience with working in self-organized teams

• Familiarity with Agile methodology

• Experience with test-driven development is a plus

Workplace

Workplace

We offer

We are committed to building a diverse and inclusive engineering team and particularly encourage applications from groups underrepres

descriptionByLocale.it: Ingegnere Sistemi – Automazione Piattaforma 80%-100%, Lugano, a tempo determinato stampa Druppo Lo Swiss National Supercomputing Centre (CSCS) sviluppa e gestisce un'infrastruttura di calcolo e di ricerca dati ad alte prestazioni che supporta la scienza di livello mondiale in Svizzera. Il suo laboratorio di utenti è disponibile per i ricercatori nazionali e internazionali in accademia, industria e settore business. Il centro è gestito da ETH Zurich e ha sede presso il suo data center di Lugano e a Zurigo. Per questa posizione la posizione di lavoro è Lugano. Sfondo del progetto Poiché le tecnologie di calcolo ad alte prestazioni, AI e cloud continuano a convergere; CSCS sta ridefinindo come i servizi computazionali avanzati sono progettati e consegnati. I moderni carichi di lavoro scientifici e ingegneristici non sono più solo grandi—sono complessi, intensivi di dati e altamente diversificati, spingendo le infrastrutture esistenti ai suoi limiti. Stiamo offrendo un contratto inizialmente limitato a due anni , che fornirà l'opportunità di contribuire a un paesaggio AI in rapida evoluzione in cui CSCS svolge un ruolo chiave e di sostenere iniziative ad alto impatto sia a livello nazionale che internazionale. Questo include i contributi all'Iniziativa dell'AI svizzera e programmi simili, come il supporto di prestito per lo sviluppo e il rilascio dei modelli di fondazione nel dominio meteo e clima. Il contratto iniziale di due anni potrebbe potenzialmente essere esteso o addirittura diventare permanente. Descrizione del lavoro L'obiettivo principale di questa posizione è quello di sviluppare e gestire i servizi HPC/AI in cima a un'infrastruttura multi-tenant. Come ingegnere di automazione della piattaforma, contribuirai direttamente alla progettazione, implementazione, manutenzione e documentazione dei servizi della piattaforma per supportare HPC e AI. Il vostro lavoro migliorerà direttamente la funzionalità e l'efficienza del sistema generale. Principali doveri: • Investigazione, risoluzione dei problemi e debug dei servizi della piattaforma e delle risorse infrastrutturali • Sviluppare, mantenere e supportare strumenti e tubazioni per supportare piattaforme su un'infrastruttura geograficamente ridondante • Sviluppare automazione per fornire, testare, distribuire e monitorare le risorse per supportare le esigenze delle piattaforme HPC e AI • Sostenere, documentare e condividere la conoscenza degli strumenti, e procedur Profilo Si dovrebbe avere un diploma di laurea o superiore in ingegneria informatica, informatica, un campo tecnico rilevante, o esperienza pratica equivalente. Si dovrebbe avere una solida conoscenza di: • Esperienza nella distribuzione delle infrastrutture HPC, AI o Cloud • Gestione dei servizi HPC/AI per massimizzare l'utilizzo di componenti di calcolo, archiviazione e rete ad alta velocità • Conoscenze di lavoro di strumenti e quadri di automazione, compresi i processi CI/CD e l'ecosistema • competenze di amministrazione Linux L'esperienza con il seguente è preferita, anche se ci saranno ampie opportunità per imparare e acquisire più esperienza con tutte queste competenze sul lavoro: • Sistemi di versione e flussi di lavoro CI/CD come ArgoCD • Debug di microservizi in esecuzione su Kubernetes • Monitoraggio delle prestazioni e strumenti diagnostici per l'hardware HPC/AI • Infrastrutture come strumenti di codice come Terraform e Ansible Qualità personali: • Giocatore di squadra automotivato e proattivo • Forte capacità di comunicazione o interesse a svilupparle • Forte mentalità problem solving con tolleranza per l'incertezza e il cambiamento • Comprende le esigenze degli utenti e lavora in collaborazione per affrontarli • Adattativo e disposto ad imparare nuove tecnologie con e da altri • Confortevoli problemi complessi o ambigui • Confortevole ammettere quando non si sa, raggiungere e sfruttare la giusta esperienza quando necessario Gestione e metodologia del progetto: • Esperienza con il lavoro in team auto-organizzati • Familiarità con la metodologia Agile • L'esperienza con lo sviluppo guidato da test è un plus Luogo di lavoro Offriamo Ci impegniamo a costruire un team di ingegneria diversificato e inclusivo e in particolare a incoraggiare le applicazioni di gruppi underreprepres

jobs.description:
DevOps Engineer

80%-100%, Lugano, fixed-term

print
Drucken

The Swiss National Supercomputing Centre (CSCS) develops and operates a high-performance computing and data research infrastructure that supports world-class science in Switzerland. Its user laboratory is available to domestic and international researchers in academia, industry, and the business sector. The centre is operated by ETH Zurich and has offices at its data centre in Lugano and in Zurich.

For this position the preferred work location is Lugano, but it could also be Zürich.

Project background

We are seeking a versatile and driven DevOps Engineer to help design, build, and operate the software-defined infrastructure and services powering advanced scientific computing and AI/ML workloads at scale.

You will work at the intersection of systems engineering, software engineering, cloud-native infrastructure, and high-performance computing (HPC), contributing to platforms and services used by researchers and engineers tackling complex scientific and AI challenges.

We value strong engineering fundamentals, curiosity, adaptability, and willingness to learn more than a perfect initial match of technical requirements. We welcome engineers from diverse backgrounds who are eager to contribute and grow. If you are motivated by challenging technical environments and enjoy understanding systems deeply, we strongly encourage you to apply even if your experience does not cover every area listed below.

We are offering a contract initially limited to two years , which will provide the opportunity to contribute to a fast-evolving AI landscape in which CSCS plays a key role and to support high-impact initiatives both nationally and internationally. This includes contributions to the Swiss AI Initiative and similar programs, such as lending support for the development and release of the Apertus models.

The initial two-year contract could potentially be extended or even become permanent.

Job description

• Design, deploy, automate, and operate scalable infrastructure and cloud-native platform services

• Contribute to Kubernetes-based AI/ML and HPC platforms, including CI/CD, GitOps, observability, security, and operational tooling

• Collaborate with researchers and engineers to support complex workflows, troubleshoot production environments, and improve reliability and performance

• Contribute to platform engineering, automation, and developer productivity initiatives across evolving systems and services

• The technologies and areas below illustrate the breadth of our environment and interests. They are not a checklist of requirements, and experience in only some of these areas is expected

Profile

The technologies and areas below illustrate the breadth of our environment and interests. They are not a checklist of requirements, and experience in only some of these areas is expected.

Technical environment and areas of interest:

• Linux systems engineering, and software development (e.g., Python, Bash)

• Containers, Kubernetes, CI/CD, GitOps, and Infrastructure as Code (e.g., Terraform, Helm, Ansible, ArgoCD)

• Distributed systems concepts, APIs, scalability, observability, identity and access management, and security

• AI/ML platforms and supporting infrastructure services

• HPC systems, GPU clusters, and large-scale infrastructure environments

• Platform engineering and developer productivity tooling

• Secure or confidentiality-sensitive operational environments

Personal qualities:

• Curious, hands-on, and eager to understand systems inside-out

• Strong engineering mindset and problem-solving attitude

• Comfortable learning new technologies and working across disciplines

• Effective communicator and collaborative team player

Ways to stand out from the crowd:

• Experience supporting research or scientific computing environments

• Familiarity with HPC systems and services

• Exposure to GPU clusters and accelerated computing

• Experience with SRE p

jobs.description:
PhD Position on Sleep, Stress and Arousal in Humans

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

A World-Class Research Environment at the Intersection of Sleep, Physiology and Health Technology

The Neural Control of Movement Lab at ETH Zurich, Department of Health Sciences and Technology, invites exceptional candidates to apply for a PhD position focused on the physiological links between sleep, stress, arousal and health in humans. The project combines mechanistic laboratory experiments with real-world, home-based and decentralized phenotyping, using multimodal physiological recordings, mobile health technologies and computational analysis pipelines.

The Neural Control of Movement Lab focuses on understanding how the brain controls behavior and on developing non-invasive interfaces to measure and modulate brain function during wake and sleep. Within this environment, the PhD student will contribute to a translational research program that aims to understand how daily stress and arousal states shape sleep physiology, recovery and health-relevant outcomes in real life.

The Department of Health Sciences and Technology at ETH Zurich unites researchers across neuroscience, biomedical engineering, movement science, nutrition, physiology and medicine. It offers an interdisciplinary environment for research at the interface of human biology, technology and clinical translation.

Project background

Sleep, stress and arousal are deeply interconnected physiological processes. Persistent stress and heightened arousal can alter the transition into sleep, change nocturnal brain and autonomic activity, and influence recovery, resilience and longer-term health. Yet many key mechanisms are still studied either in tightly controlled laboratory settings or through simplified real-world measures that do not capture the richness of human physiology.

This project addresses that gap by combining mechanistic in-lab studies with real-world phenotyping of sleep, stress and arousal in daily life. The goal is to develop rigorous, scalable research workflows that can measure how stress and arousal unfold across the day, how they affect sleep and overnight recovery, and which physiological signatures are most informative for health-relevant phenotypes.

The project will use multimodal biosignal acquisition, such as pupillometry, sleep EEG, ECG, respiration, wearable and actigraphy data, smartphone-supported assessments and validated questionnaires, together with advanced signal processing, statistical modelling and machine learning. The PhD student will help implement, coordinate and analyze studies that bridge controlled physiology and ecological, home-based assessment.

The successful candidate will design, conduct and analyze human studies linking sleep, stress, arousal and autonomic physiology in both laboratory and real-world settings. The position is ideal for a candidate who wants to combine hands-on human physiology, sleep research, mobile health methods and strong computational data analysis. Professional software engineers may support parts of the technical backbone, but the PhD student should be able to implement and understand the data flow, work with technical collaborators, implement research-facing pipelines and take scientific ownership of the physiological data and its interpretation.

Your work will include:

• Design and conduct mechanistic laboratory studies and real-world sleep, stress and arousal studies in human participants

• C

Il progetto combina esperimenti di laboratorio meccanicistici con fenotipazione reale, basata sulla casa e decentralizzata, utilizzando registrazioni fisiologiche multimodali, tecnologie sanitarie mobili e condotte di analisi computazionali. Il Neural Control of Movement Lab si concentra sulla comprensione del modo in cui il cervello controlla il comportamento e sullo sviluppo di interfacce non invasive per misurare e modulare la funzione cerebrale durante la veglia e il sonno. All'interno di questo ambiente, lo studente di dottorato contribuirà a un programma di ricerca traduttiva che mira a capire come lo stress quotidiano e gli stati eccitanti modellano la fisiologia del sonno, il recupero e risultati rilevanti per la salute nella vita reale. Il Dipartimento di Scienze della Salute e Tecnologia dell'ETH Zurigo unisce ricercatori in neuroscienze, ingegneria biomedica, scienza del movimento, nutrizione, fisiologia e medicina. Offre un ambiente interdisciplinare per la ricerca nell'interfaccia della biologia umana, della tecnologia e della traduzione clinica. Sfondo del progetto Il sonno, lo stress e l'eccitazione sono processi fisiologici profondamente interconnessi. Lo stress persistente e l'eccitazione accresciuta possono alterare la transizione nel sonno, cambiare il cervello notturno e l'attività autonoma, e influenzare il recupero, la resilienza e la salute a più lungo termine. Il progetto utilizzerà l'acquisizione multimodale di biosignal, come la lotteria degli alunni, l'EEG del sonno, l'ECG, la respirazione, i dati indossabili e l'attigrafia, le valutazioni supportate dagli smartphone e i questionari convalidati, insieme all'elaborazione avanzata del segnale, alla modellazione statistica e all'apprendimento delle macchine. Lo studente di dottorato aiuterà a implementare, coordinare e analizzare studi che controllano la fisiologia del ponte e la valutazione ecologica, basata sulla casa. descriptionByLocale.fr: Descrizione Position du doctorat sur le sommeil, le stress et l'excitation chez les humains 100%, Zurich, durée déterminée imprimer Drucken Un environnement de recherche de calibre mondial à l'intersection des technologies du sommeil, de la physiologie et de la santé Le Neural Control of Movement Lab de l'ETH Zurich, Département des sciences et technologies de la santé, invite des candidats exceptionnels à postuler à un poste de doctorat axé sur les liens physiologiques entre le sommeil, le stress, l'excitation et la santé chez l'homme. Le projet combine des expériences de laboratoire mécanistes avec le phénotypage réel, à domicile et décentralisé, en utilisant des enregistrements physiologiques multimodaux, des technologies de santé mobiles et des pipelines d'analyse computationnelle. Le Neural Control of Movement Lab se concentre sur la compréhension de la façon dont le cerveau contrôle le comportement et sur le développement d'interfaces non invasives pour mesurer et moduler la fonction cérébrale pendant le réveil et le sommeil. Dans ce contexte, le doctorant contribuera à un programme de recherche translationnelle qui vise à comprendre comment le stress quotidien et les états d'excitation façonnent la physiologie du sommeil, le rétablissement et les résultats pertinents pour la santé dans la vie réelle. Le Département des sciences de la santé et de la technologie de l'ETH Zurich réunit des chercheurs dans les domaines des neurosciences, de l'ingénierie biomédicale, des sciences du mouvement, de la nutrition, de la physiologie et de la médecine. Il offre un environnement interdisciplinaire pour la recherche à l'interface de la biologie humaine, de la technologie et de la traduction clinique. Contexte du projet Le sommeil, le stress et l'excitation sont des processus physiologiques profondément interconnectés. Le stress persistant et l'excitation accrue peuvent modifier la transition vers le sommeil, changer le cerveau nocturne et l'activité autonome, et influencer la récupération, la résilience et la santé à long terme. Pourtant, de nombreux mécanismes clés sont encore étudiés soit dans des laboratoires étroitement contrôlés, soit par des mesures simplifiées du monde réel qui ne saisissent pas la richesse de la physiologie humaine. Ce projet vise à combler cette lacune en combinant des études mécanistes en laboratoire avec le phénotypage réel du sommeil, du stress et de l'excitation dans la vie quotidienne. L'objectif est d'élaborer des flux de travail de recherche rigoureux et évolutifs qui permettent de mesurer comment le stress et l'excitation se déroulent au cours de la journée, comment ils affectent le sommeil et la récupération du jour au lendemain, et quelles signatures physiologiques sont les plus informatives pour les phénotypes pertinents pour la santé. Le projet utilisera l'acquisition de biosignaux multimodaux, tels que la pupillométrie, l'EEG du sommeil, l'ECG, la respiration, les données portables et actigraphiques, les évaluations soutenues par smartphone et les questionnaires validés, ainsi que le traitement avancé des signaux, la modélisation statistique et l'apprentissage automatique. Le doctorant aidera à mettre en oeuvre, coordonner et analyser les études qui relient la physiologie contrôlée et l'évaluation écologique à domicile. Description du poste Le candidat retenu concevra, mènera et analysera des études humaines sur le sommeil, le stress, l'excitation et la physiologie autonome en laboratoire et dans le monde réel. Un élément central de la position sera la mise en place de pipelines de recherche robustes pour le phénotypage mobile et décentralisé, y compris les flux de travail de collecte de données, le traitement des biosignales, le contrôle de la qualité, la synchronisation, l'extraction de fonctionnalités et l'analyse computationnelle. Le poste est idéal pour un candidat qui veut combiner la physiologie humaine pratique, la recherche sur le sommeil, les méthodes de santé mobiles et une analyse de données computationnelles solide. Les ingénieurs en logiciels professionnels peuvent soutenir des parties de l'épine dorsale technique, mais le doctorant devrait être en mesure de mettre en œuvre et de comprendre le flux de données, de travailler avec des collaborateurs techniques, de mettre en place des pipelines faisant face à la recherche et de s'approprier scientifiquement les données physiologiques et leur interprétation. Mansioni - Concevoir et mener des études de laboratoire mécanistes et des études sur le sommeil, le stress et l'excitation dans le monde réel chez les participants humains - Acquérir et gérer des données physiologiques multimodales pendant le sillage et le sommeil telles que pupillométrie, EEG, ECG, respiration, photopléthysmographie, actigraphie, données de capteur portable, évaluations basées sur smartphone et questionnaires - C

jobs.description:
Doctoral Position in AI-Assisted Bridge Assessment for Special Road Transports

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

This project combines classical structural analysis with modern data-based and computational methods (AI & FEM) to advance the structural assessment of bridges under special road transports.

• A fully funded doctoral position at the Chair of Structural Engineering - Concrete Structures and Bridge Design (Prof. Walter Kaufmann), ETH Zurich

• In collaboration with the Computational Design Lab (Prof. B. Bickel), the ETH AI Center and Design++

• With direct practical relevance for Swiss infrastructure and the Swiss Federal Roads Office (ASTRA) as industry partner

Project background

The Swiss Federal Roads Office (ASTRA) processes more than 20,000 applications for special road transports every year — vehicles or vehicle combinations that exceed the legal limits. Roughly half of these applications require a structural assessment of the bridges along the route. Given the high number of applications and the diversity of transport configurations and bridge inventories that need to be considered, this manual assessment is correspondingly time-intensive. This research project explores how methods from Artificial Intelligence (AI) and automation can complement and further develop the structural assessment of existing bridges under heavy transportation loads. Starting from established engineering practice, we investigate:

• Which parametric models and which representations of the most common bridge types allow us to assess structural safety and serviceability efficiently for special road transports?

• How can simulation data and bridge inventory data be combined so that data-driven models remain mechanically consistent, reliable, and interpretable?

• How can the influence of recurring heavy transports on structural damage and therefore on the durability of the structure be meaningfully captured in such models?

Job description

• Independent research exploring how methods from AI and automation can complement and further develop the structural assessment of existing bridges under heavy transportation loads

• Regular exchange with the industry partner ASTRA (Swiss Federal Roads Office) to ensure practical relevance

• Scientific writing of a doctoral thesis as well as peer-reviewed journal and conference publications, with the opportunity to attend leading international conferences in the field

• Support of teaching activities at the Chair & co-supervision of Bachelor's and Master's theses within the thematic scope of the position

• Completion of 12 course credits in the research field as part of the doctoral programme

Profile

• You enjoy working at the intersection of classical structural engineering and modern data- and computer-aided methods

• You hold a Master's degree in Civil Engineering, preferably with a specialisation in Structural Engineering

• Ideally you also have experience in scripting (Python) and AI/ Machine Learning / Data Science

• You work independently and with high initiative

• You communicate your work clearly in English, both in writing and in exchange with academic and industry partners (German is a plus)

Workplace

Workplace

We offer

• Supervision by Prof. Walter Kaufmann and Dr. Sophia Kuhn (Postdoc, computational design lab ).

• As part of a chair associated with the ETH AI Center , the opportunity to become an associated researcher and join its community

• Additionally, access to the community of the Center for Augmented Computational Design in Architecture, Engineering and Construction (Design++)

• A range of career development programmes, with mentors from both industry and academia

• A great working environment and a supportive group, according to former doctoral students

jobs.description:
Financial and administrative officer

60%-80%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

The NCCR CLIM+ is a new National Center of Competence in Research that is establishing the first fully interdisciplinary, Switzerland-wide climate research community that tackles pressing issues related to climate extremes such as heatwaves, floods, heavy rainfalls, droughts, wildfires, and further compound events. It will thereby interact with stakeholders ranging from public health to finance, agriculture, and water management. tp produce actionable climate solution pathways related to adaptation and mitigation, forming a new transdisciplinary nexus between science, society, practice, and politics.

Project background

NCCR CLIM+ is led by ETH Zurich and the University of Bern, and includes 20 partner institutions across Switzerland. At ETH Zurich, NCCR CLIM+ is led by Prof. Sonia I. Seneviratne and Prof. David N. Bresch, with a total involvement of 17 professors and research groups from 8 departments. The other leading house is the University of Bern (co-director: Prof. Karin Ingold; deputy co-director: Prof. Olivia Romppainen-Martius). In total, the NCCR CLIM+ has 57 project partners from a range of institutions from Switzerland. The first phase of NCCR CLIM+ is planned until April 30, 2030, with a possible extension for an additional 4–8 years (up to 12 years in total). NCCR CLIM+ will also lead the development of a newly founded long-term Center for Climate Extremes and Resilience in Swiss Society (CERESS).

Further information about NCCR CLIM+ can be found on our website .

Job description

The Financial and administrative officer position is part of the NCCR CLIM+ Management Center, which is headed by an Executive manager. The Management Center also includes a Communications Officer, as well as Technical and Scientific officers from the NCCR CLIM+. The main responsibilities of the NCCR CLIM+ Financial and administrative officer will be as follows:

• Establishment of the NCCR CLIM+ Management Center at ETH Zurich in collaboration with the Executive Manager, as well as Prof. Sonia I. Seneviratne and Prof. David N. Bresch

• Budget management and accounting of NCCR CLIM+, including distribution and financial controlling of SNSF funds allocated to the principal investigators of NCCR CLIM+

• Budget management and accounting of ETH Zurich funding within NCCR CLIM+, including financial controlling

• Financial reports for SNSF and ETH Zurich

• Financial, human resources, and general administration of the Management Center

• Timely execution of all activities and services in accordance with the SNSF' and ETH Zurich’s guidelines and process requirements

• Correspondence and communication with the Swiss National Science Foundation (SNSF), ETH Zurich Administration, and NCCR CLIM+ PIs on financial and administrative matters

• Co-organization of site visits, conferences, workshops, reports, and proposals in collaboration with NCCR CLIM+ Executive Manager, as well as Prof. Sonia I. Seneviratne and Prof. David N. Bresch

Profile

• Demonstrated expertise and experience in finance management and budget controlling

• High degree of autonomy

• Excellent command of English (written and spoken)

• Excellent command of German (written and spoken)

• Expertise and experience in administrative management (particularly finance and human resources)

• Expertise and experience in event management and reporting

• Solid computer skills (office, internet, budget accounting); ability to use programs and applications to solve complex problems and tasks quickly and independently

• Efficient and precise work style

• Sense of responsibility, quick learner, ability to take initiative, and organizational skills

• Interpersonal skills, flexibility, and ability to work under pressure

• Experience with university administrative processes is a plus

• Experience in the administration of interdisciplinary research projects is a plus

• Teamplayer

jobs.description:
PhD Position in Microfluidics for Assembly of Synthetic Cells for Energy Production, Nutrient Metabolism and Molecular Transport

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

The deMello Group in the Department of Chemistry and Applied Biosciences at ETH Zürich, a world-leading group for the development of novel microfluidic technologies, is looking for a motivated PhD student in cutting-edge research in microfluidics and synthetic biology.

Project background

Living systems rely on continuous energy conversion to maintain vital functions, transforming external energy sources into biochemical units like ATP and NAD(P)H to power metabolic processes. One approach to understanding this complexity is to reconstruct a cell from scratch using a minimal set of components, i.e., to build a synthetic cell. In synthetic biology, micrometer-sized lipid vesicles can serve as artificial cells, providing a platform to reconstruct and manipulate essential biological functions. However, current methods to generate giant unilamellar vesicles (GUVs) face challenges such as size heterogeneity, inefficient membrane protein reconstitution, and limited compartmentalization. Overcoming these limitations is essential for engineering self-sustaining synthetic cells that can autonomously regulate energy metabolism and biochemical processes.

Our approach integrates microfluidic precision with synthetic biology to engineer synthetic cells that autonomously regulate energy metabolism and biochemical processes. This interdisciplinary research is conducted in collaboration between ETH Zürich (Dr. Stavrakis) and the University of Bern (Prof. von Ballmoos). The outcomes will pave the way for innovative applications in biotechnology, biosensing, and synthetic bioengineering, contributing fundamentally to the design and fabrication of programmable living systems.

Job description

We are seeking a highly motivated PhD candidate to develop microfluidic platforms for reconstituting functional membrane proteins into lipid vesicles. The project combines microfluidics, super-resolution fluorescence imaging, and membrane protein biophysics to engineer synthetic cells that will autonomously regulate energy metabolism, biochemical synthesis, and nutrient transport, mimicking natural cellular homeostasis.

Key Responsibilities

• Establish microfluidic platforms for controlled fabrication of monodisperse synthetic vesicles with tunable membrane properties

• Develop microfluidic strategies for membrane protein reconstitution into synthetic vesicle membranes

• Work closely with both the Zurich and Bern groups, including microfluidics setup and preparation of fluorescently labelled membrane proteins

• Perform super-resolution microscopy of membrane proteins in the synthetic vesicles

The project is highly interdisciplinary, fostering close collaboration with biochemists and biophysicists, to accelerate the design and fabrication of programmable living systems.

Profile

• The successful candidate should hold an MSc degree in chemistry, biophysics, chemical or bio-engineering with first class grades

• Basic experience in microfabrication and microfluidics, biophysics, cell biology will be beneficial

• Fluent communication skills (written and presentation) in English are essential

• The PhD candidate will join an excellent and highly ambitious teams at the forefront of research in the areas of microfluidics and synthetic biology

descriptionByLocale.fr: Doctorat en microfluidique pour l'assemblage de cellules synthétiques pour la production d'énergie, le métabolisme des nutriments et le transport moléculaire 100%, Zurich, durée déterminée imprimer Drucken Le groupe deMello du Département de chimie et de biosciences appliquées de l'ETH Zürich, un groupe mondial de pointe pour le développement de nouvelles technologies microfluidiques, recherche un doctorant motivé en recherche de pointe en microfluidique et en biologie synthétique. Contexte du projet Les systèmes vivants comptent sur la conversion continue d'énergie pour maintenir des fonctions vitales, transformant les sources d'énergie externes en unités biochimiques comme l'ATP et le NAD(P)H pour alimenter les processus métaboliques. Une approche pour comprendre cette complexité consiste à reconstruire une cellule à partir de zéro en utilisant un ensemble minimal de composants, c.-à-d., pour construire une cellule synthétique. En biologie synthétique, les vésicules lipidiques de taille micrométrique peuvent servir de cellules artificielles, fournissant une plate-forme pour reconstruire et manipuler les fonctions biologiques essentielles. Cependant, les méthodes actuelles pour générer des vésicules monolamellaires géantes (VGU) sont confrontées à des défis tels que l'hétérogénéité de la taille, la reconstitution inefficace des protéines membranaires et la compartimentation limitée. Surmonter ces limites est essentiel pour l'ingénierie des cellules synthétiques autosuffisantes qui peuvent réguler de façon autonome le métabolisme énergétique et les processus biochimiques. Notre approche intègre la précision microfluidique à la biologie synthétique pour concevoir des cellules synthétiques qui régulent de façon autonome le métabolisme énergétique et les processus biochimiques. Cette recherche interdisciplinaire est menée en collaboration entre ETH Zürich (Dr Stavrakis) et l'Université de Berne (Prof. von Ballmoos). Les résultats ouvriront la voie à des applications novatrices en biotechnologie, en biosension et en bioingénierie synthétique, contribuant fondamentalement à la conception et à la fabrication de systèmes vivants programmables. Description du poste Nous recherchons un doctorant très motivé pour développer des plates-formes microfluidiques pour reconstituer des protéines membranaires fonctionnelles en vésicules lipidiques. Le projet combine la microfluidique, l'imagerie par fluorescence à super-résolution et la biophysique des protéines membranaires pour concevoir des cellules synthétiques qui réguleront de façon autonome le métabolisme de l'énergie, la synthèse biochimique et le transport des éléments nutritifs, en imitant l'homéostasie cellulaire naturelle. Principales responsabilités • Mettre en place des plates-formes microfluidiques pour la fabrication contrôlée de vésicules synthétiques monodispersées ayant des propriétés membranaires thoneuses • Développer des stratégies microfluidiques de reconstitution des protéines membranaires en membranes vésiculeuses synthétiques • Travailler en étroite collaboration avec les groupes Zurich et Berne, y compris la mise en place de microfluidiques et la préparation de protéines membranaires marquées fluorescentement • Effectuer la microscopie super-résolution des protéines membranaires dans les vésicules synthétiques Le projet est hautement interdisciplinaire, favorisant une collaboration étroite avec les biochimistes et les biophysiciens, pour accélérer la conception et la fabrication de systèmes de vie programmables. Profil • Le candidat retenu devrait être titulaire d'un diplôme de maîtrise en chimie, biophysique, chimique ou bioingénierie avec des grades de première classe • Une expérience de base en microfabrication et en microfluidique, biophysique, biologie cellulaire sera bénéfique • Les compétences de communication (écrites et présentées) en anglais sont essentielles • Le doctorant se joindra à une excellente et très ambitieuse équipe à la pointe de la recherche dans les domaines de la microfluidique et de la biologie synthétique Lieu de travail Nous offrons • Votre travail avec impact: Devenez membre de l'ETH Zurich, qui non seulement soutient votre développement professionnel, mais contribue également activement au changement positif dans la société • Vous pouvez vous attendre à de nombreux avantages , tels que les billets de saison de transport public et le partage de voiture , un large éventail de sports offerts par l'ASVZ , garde d'enfants et prestations de retraite attrayantes chevron droit Travail, enseignement et recherche à l'ETH Zurich Nous apprécions la diversité et la durabilité Conformément à nos valeurs , ETH Zurich encourage

jobs.description:
Postdoctoral Position in Stakeholder Engagement

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

We invite applications for a postdoctoral position at the Transdisciplinarity-Lab (TdLab) of the Department of Environmental Systems Science at ETH Zürich. You will be responsible for designing and implementing the stakeholder engagement of the NCCR CLIM+.

Project background

The postdoctoral position will be an integral part of the newly established National Competence Centre in Research NCCR CLIM+ . NCCR CLIM+ supports Switzerland’s transformation towards a climate-resilient society and trains a new generation of experts with strong disciplinary and transdisciplinary expertise. This project offers the opportunity to collaborate with leading experts in atmospheric and climate science within the NCCR CLIM+ as well as ETH Zurich.

Job description

In the NCCR CLIM+ storylines are key to achieve actionable knowledge and cross-disciplinary communication. Storylines are scientifically based stories that represent plausible futures and extreme climate outcomes in their physical and social dimensions. You will be responsible to embed the storylines in their societal environment. For each storyline you will

• Identify the most important stakeholders and establish a network that connects them with the storyline’s researchers.

• Develop, implement and evaluate a Theory of Change with the network.

• Design, implement and evaluate the transdisciplinary process of engagement and co-production of knowledge and practices.

You are welcome to further develop transdisciplinary methods and theories and to make your achievements known via talks and publications.

The position is for three years initially and can be extended. The starting date is as soon as possible.

In general, doctoral / postdoctoral researchers at ETH Zurich have a full-time employment. A part-time employment may only be considered in exceptional cases (e.g. child- or familycare, other projects or employment).

Profile

We are looking for a person who

• Has a doctorate in environmental or sustainability sciences.

• Is experienced in designing, implementing and evaluating transdisciplinary research processes.

• Has excellent interpersonal skills for both, collaborating with researchers of different disciplines as well as with stakeholders of different sectors of society.

• Can handle situations of conflicting communication, power and interests, looking for a pragmatic way forward.

• Is interested in critically questioning transdisciplinary theories and methods to develop them further.

• Is fluent in English and German.

Workplace

We offer

TdLab’s expertise lies in theories and practices of transdisciplinary research and teaching. We offer a work environment that invites you to take ownership of your project, while getting skilled support as needed. We are looking for collaborators who want to further develop transdisciplinary research and teaching with a mindset of failing forward. Your future colleagues have diverse disciplinary backgrounds. They work with theories and practices of transdisciplinary research and teaching as a means to promote sustainable development.

Working, teaching and research at ETH Zurich

We value diversity and sustainability

In line with our values , ETH Zurich encourages an inclusive culture. We promote equality of opportunity, value diversity and nurture a working and learning environment in which the rights and dignity of all our staff and students are respected. Visit our Equal Opportunities and Diversity website to find out how we ensure a fair and open environment that allows everyone to grow and flourish. Sustainability is a core value for us – we are consistently working towards a climate-neutral future .

Curious? So are we.

We look forward to receiving your online application with the following documents:

• Motivation letter

• CV, including certificates for your studies and PhD

• A short

jobs.description:
Postdoctoral researcher in optimization for robust railway timetables

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

Despite the excellent quality of public transport systems in Switzerland, the railway system needs to increase its performance (quality, for instance, travel time, and delays) and capacity (amount of services run) and attract more travellers to match the ambitious targets from policy and environmental goals. One key aspect of traditional railway transport systems is their plan, which is based on predetermined routes, lines, and scheduled times, with little possibility of adjusting to unplanned and unexpected circumstances. On the other hand, delays and disruption might affect many services throughout a network by means of propagation. The project focuses on timetable planning that is able to minimize delays and their impacts.

To do so, large-scale optimisation addresses the railway timetabling problem. Typically Mixed Integer Linear Programming approaches are used, which are mathematically complex, and with some limits, when modelling real-life complexity. Incorporating robustness against delays is an additional important aspect. This project assumes that we are able to quantify how small delays develop and propagate throughout the network; how larger disruptions develop and propagate in the network. Given this, we want to determine robust timetables, with suitable choice of buffers and running time reserves. Those timetables, under delays, are able to perform quantitatively better (i.e. less delays, fewer larger delays,...).

This position will be available, with an ideal starting date between September 2026 and April 2027, or further upon agreement; the planned duration of the initial contract is one year, to be extended based on successful performance, for up to 2 years.

Project background

The focus of this project is to understand how delays occur and propagate in a real-life railway network. This exposes some complex dynamics as response to external events (small delays, larger disruptions), and some impact, which can be characterized by simulation models. The scientific challenge involves designing timetabling models that can deal with the complexity of existing system dynamics, in a variety of integrative aspects.

The project is designed in collaboration with industry player operating as railway infrastructure manager. The project bases on available solvers for non-periodic timetabling, which include MILP and Logic-Based Benders-Decomposition approaches. This research is carried out within an international cooperation with the Complex Systems group at Utrecht University, in the Netherlands.

Job description

• expand and consolidate existing timetabling models to include constraints from limited resources; and complex dynamics resulting from variable choices.

• expand scope of scheduling models to tackle multi objective problems, and non-scalar objective functions (like probability of delays).

• study local and systemic impacts of timetables when exposed to expected or speculative delay dynamics.

Profile

Ideally, you have (or are about to receive) a Doctoral Degree in transport sciences, management/ decision sciences, applied mathematics, econometrics, statistics, computer science, physics or related fields.

Your research track is consistent and shows a track record, or clear potential, for analysing, modelling, control, and optimisation of transport systems. You are highly motivated and self-driven, with a clear research vision, academic ambition, and excellent communication and writing skills (fluent spoken and written English is mandatory). Moreover, the following skills are expected of a promising candidate:

• Computer science and ability to program independently complex software

• Ability to model and work with algorithmic design, existing software and data provided by industrial partners

• Knowledge of mathematical optimisation (MILP, IP, LP) and/or control sciences

• Team working and commun

Ricercatore post-dottorato in ottimizzazione per robusti orari ferroviari 100%, Zurigo, a tempo determinato stampa Druppo Nonostante l'eccellente qualità dei sistemi di trasporto pubblico in Svizzera, il sistema ferroviario deve aumentare le sue prestazioni (qualità, ad esempio, tempi di viaggio e ritardi) e la capacità (importo dei servizi gestiti) e attirare più viaggiatori per soddisfare gli obiettivi ambiziosi da obiettivi politici e ambientali. Un aspetto chiave dei tradizionali sistemi di trasporto ferroviario è il loro piano, che si basa su percorsi predeterminati, linee e tempi programmati, con poca possibilità di adattarsi a circostanze non pianificate e inaspettate. D'altra parte, ritardi e interruzioni potrebbero influenzare molti servizi in tutta una rete per mezzo di propagazione. Il progetto si concentra sulla pianificazione degli orari che è in grado di minimizzare i ritardi e i loro impatti. Per farlo, l'ottimizzazione su larga scala affronta il problema del timetabling ferroviario. In genere vengono utilizzati approcci di programmazione lineare Integer Misti, matematicamente complessi, e con alcuni limiti, quando si modella la complessità della vita reale. Incorporare robustezza contro ritardi è un ulteriore aspetto importante. Questo progetto presuppone che siamo in grado di quantificare come piccoli ritardi si sviluppano e si propagano in tutta la rete; come le interruzioni più grandi si sviluppano e si propagano nella rete. Dato questo, vogliamo determinare orari robusti, con una scelta adeguata di buffer e riserve di tempo di esecuzione. Quei orari, in ritardo, sono in grado di eseguire quantitativamente meglio (cioè meno ritardi, meno ritardi,...). Questa posizione sarà disponibile, con una data di partenza ideale tra il settembre 2026 e l'aprile 2027, o più avanti d'accordo; la durata prevista del contratto iniziale è di un anno, da estendere sulla base di prestazioni di successo, fino a 2 anni. Sfondo del progetto L'obiettivo di questo progetto è capire come si verificano ritardi e si propagano in una rete ferroviaria di vita reale. Questo espone alcune dinamiche complesse come risposta ad eventi esterni (piccoli ritardi, interruzioni più grandi), e qualche impatto, che può essere caratterizzato da modelli di simulazione. La sfida scientifica consiste nella progettazione di modelli di timetabling in grado di affrontare la complessità delle dinamiche di sistema esistenti, in una varietà di aspetti integrativi. Il progetto è progettato in collaborazione con i player del settore che operano come responsabile delle infrastrutture ferroviarie. Le basi di progetto sui risolutori disponibili per il timetabling non periodico, che includono gli approcci MILP e Logic-Based Benders-Decomposition. Questa ricerca si svolge all'interno di una cooperazione internazionale con il gruppo Complex Systems dell'Università Utrecht, nei Paesi Bassi. Descrizione del lavoro
• espandere e consolidare i modelli di timetabling esistenti per includere vincoli da risorse limitate; e dinamiche complesse derivanti da scelte variabili.
• espandere la portata dei modelli di programmazione per affrontare i problemi multi oggettivi, e le funzioni oggettive non-scalari (come la probabilità di ritardi).
• studiare gli impatti locali e sistemici degli orari quando esposti alle dinamiche di ritardo previste o speculative. Profilo Idealmente, hai (o stai per ricevere) un Dottorato in scienze dei trasporti, scienze della gestione / decisioni, matematica applicata, econometria, statistiche, informatica, fisica o campi correlati. La vostra pista di ricerca è coerente e mostra un track record, o un potenziale chiaro, per analizzare, modellare, controllare e ottimizzare i sistemi di trasporto. Sei altamente motivato e auto-guidato, con una chiara visione di ricerca, ambizione accademica, e eccellenti capacità di comunicazione e scrittura (il fluente parlato e scritto inglese è obbligatorio). Inoltre, sono previste le seguenti competenze di un candidato promettente:
• Scienza informatica e capacità di programma software indipendente complesso
• Capacità di modellare e lavorare con design algoritmico, software e dati esistenti forniti da partner industriali
• Conoscenza delle scienze matematiche di ottimizzazione (MILP, IP, LP) e/o controllo
• Lavoro di squadra e commun

Postdoctoral-Forscher in Optimierung für robuste Bahnfahrpläne 100%, Zürich, befristet Drucken Drucken Trotz der ausgezeichneten Qualität der öffentlichen Verkehrssysteme in der Schweiz muss das Eisenbahnsystem seine Leistungsfähigkeit (z.B. Fahrzeit, Verzögerungen) und Kapazität (die Zahl der Dienstleistungen) erhöhen und Reisende mehr anlocken, um den ambitionierten Zielen von politischen und umweltpolitischen Zielen gerecht zu werden. Ein wesentlicher Aspekt der traditionellen Eisenbahnverkehrssysteme ist ihr Plan, der auf vorgegebenen Strecken, Linien und geplanten Zeiten basiert, mit wenig Möglichkeit, sich auf unplanmäßige und unerwartete Umstände einzustellen. Auf der anderen Seite könnten Verzögerungen und Störungen viele Dienste in einem Netzwerk durch Verbreitung beeinflussen. Das Projekt konzentriert sich auf die Planung von Fahrplänen, die Verzögerungen und deren Auswirkungen minimieren können. Zu diesem Zweck befasst sich die groß angelegte Optimierung mit dem eisenbahnbrechenden Problem. Typischerweise werden gemischte Integer Linear Programming-Ansätze verwendet, die mathematisch komplex sind und mit einigen Grenzen, bei der Modellierung der realen Komplexität. Ein weiterer wichtiger Aspekt ist die Robustheit gegen Verzögerungen. Dieses Projekt geht davon aus, dass wir in der Lage sind, zu quantifizieren, wie sich kleine Verzögerungen im gesamten Netzwerk entwickeln und propagieren; wie sich größere Störungen im Netzwerk entwickeln und propagieren. Dabei wollen wir robuste Zeitpläne mit geeigneter Wahl von Puffern und Laufzeitreserven bestimmen. Diese Zeitpläne können unter Verzögerungen quantitativ besser durchgeführt werden (d.h. weniger Verzögerungen, weniger größere Verzögerungen,...). Diese Position wird mit einem idealen Starttermin zwischen dem 20. September 2026 und dem 20. April 27 oder weiter nach Vereinbarung zur Verfügung stehen; die geplante Laufzeit des ersten Vertrags beträgt ein Jahr, um auf Basis erfolgreicher Leistungen um bis zu 2 Jahre verlängert zu werden. Projekt Hintergrund Der Schwerpunkt dieses Projekts ist, zu verstehen, wie Verzögerungen auftreten und sich in einem realen Eisenbahnnetz verbreiten. Dies zeigt einige komplexe Dynamiken als Reaktion auf externe Ereignisse (kleine Verzögerungen, größere Störungen) und einige Auswirkungen, die durch Simulationsmodelle charakterisiert werden können. Die wissenschaftliche Herausforderung besteht darin, Zeiterfassungsmodelle zu entwerfen, die sich mit der Komplexität bestehender Systemdynamik in unterschiedlichen integrativen Aspekten befassen können. Das Projekt ist in Zusammenarbeit mit dem als Eisenbahninfrastrukturmanager tätigen Industrieplayer konzipiert. Das Projekt basiert auf verfügbaren Solvents für nicht-periodische Zeitvertreibungen, darunter MILP und Logic-Based Benders-Decomposition Ansätze. Diese Forschung wird in einer internationalen Zusammenarbeit mit der Gruppe Complex Systems an der Universität Utrecht in den Niederlanden durchgeführt. Jobbeschreibung
• Ausbau und Konsolidierung bestehender Zeiterfassungsmodelle, um Einschränkungen aus begrenzten Ressourcen einzubeziehen; und komplexe Dynamiken, die sich aus variablen Entscheidungen ergeben.
• den Umfang der Planungsmodelle erweitern, um mehr objektive Probleme zu lösen, und nicht-skalare objektive Funktionen (wie Wahrscheinlichkeit von Verzögerungen).
• lokale und systemische Auswirkungen von Fahrplänen zu untersuchen, wenn sie einer erwarteten oder spekulativen Verzögerungsdynamik ausgesetzt sind. Profil Idealerweise haben Sie einen Doktorandenabschluss in Transportwissenschaften, Management/Entscheidungswissenschaften, angewandte Mathematik, Ökonometrie, Statistik, Informatik, Physik oder verwandten Bereichen. Ihr Forschungspfad ist konsistent und zeigt einen Rekord oder ein klares Potenzial für die Analyse, Modellierung, Steuerung und Optimierung von Transportsystemen. Sie sind hoch motiviert und selbstfahrend, mit einer klaren Forschungsvision, akademischem Ehrgeiz und exzellenten Kommunikations- und Schreibfähigkeiten ( fließendes gesprochenes und geschriebenes Englisch ist obligatorisch). • Informatik und Fähigkeit, unabhängig komplexe Software zu programmieren
• Fähigkeit, mit algorithmischem Design, bestehender Software und Daten von Industriepartnern zu modellieren und zu arbeiten

Chercheur postdoctoral en optimisation pour des horaires ferroviaires robustes 100%, Zurich, durée déterminée imprimer Purée Malgré l'excellente qualité des systèmes de transport en commun en Suisse, le système ferroviaire doit améliorer ses performances (qualité, par exemple, temps de déplacement et retards) et sa capacité (nombre de services offerts) et attirer davantage de voyageurs pour atteindre les objectifs ambitieux de politique et d'environnement. Un aspect clé des systèmes de transport ferroviaire traditionnels est leur plan, qui est basé sur des itinéraires, des lignes et des horaires prédéterminés, avec peu de possibilités d'adaptation aux circonstances imprévues et imprévues. D'autre part, les retards et les perturbations pourraient affecter de nombreux services à travers un réseau par la propagation. Le projet met l'accent sur la planification du calendrier qui permet de minimiser les retards et leurs répercussions. Pour ce faire, l'optimisation à grande échelle s'attaque au problème de la chronologie ferroviaire. Les approches de programmation linéaire intégrales généralement mixtes sont utilisées, qui sont mathématiquement complexes, et avec certaines limites, lors de la modélisation de la complexité de la vie réelle. L'incorporation de la robustesse contre les retards est un autre aspect important. Ce projet suppose que nous sommes en mesure de quantifier la façon dont les petits retards se développent et se propagent dans l'ensemble du réseau; comment les perturbations plus importantes se développent et se propagent dans le réseau. Compte tenu de cela, nous voulons déterminer des calendriers robustes, avec un choix approprié de tampons et de réserves de temps de fonctionnement.
