jobs.description:
Doctoral researcher in optimization for robust railway timetables

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

Despite the excellent quality of public transport systems in Switzerland, the railway system needs to increase its performance (quality, for instance, travel time, and delays) and capacity (amount of services run) and attract more travellers to match the ambitious targets from policy and environmental goals. One key aspect of traditional railway transport systems is their plan, which is based on predetermined routes, lines, and scheduled times, with little possibility of adjusting to unplanned and unexpected circumstances. On the other hand, delays and disruption might affect many services throughout a network by means of propagation. The project focuses on timetable planning that is able to minimize delays and their impacts.

To do so, large-scale optimisation addresses the railway timetabling problem. Typically Mixed Integer Linear Programming approaches are used, which are mathematically complex, and with some limits, when modelling real-life complexity. Incorporating robustness against delays is an additional important aspect. This project assumes that we are able to quantify how small delays develop and propagate throughout the network; how larger disruptions develop and propagate in the network. Given this, we want to determine robust timetables, with suitable choice of buffers and running time reserves. Those timetables, under delays, are able to perform quantitatively better (i.e. less delays, fewer larger delays,...).

This position will be available, with an ideal starting date between August 2026 and February 2027, or further upon agreement; the planned duration of the initial contract is 18 months, after which an aptitude colloquium will determine the further continuation of the doctoral project. The total doctoral project is expected to be finished in 4 years in total.

Project background

The focus of this project is to understand how different timetables result in complex dynamics as response to external events (small delays, larger disruptions). The scientific challenge involves integrating those dynamics into existing timetabling models, to identify those timetables that are actually better, under delays. This research targets improvement of timetable planning models, adjusting the amount and placement of buffers, and reserve times.

The project is designed in collaboration with industry player operating as railway infrastructure manager. The project bases on available solvers for non-periodic timetabling, which include MILP and Logic-Based Benders-Decomposition approaches. This research is carried out within an international cooperation with the Complex Systems group at Utrecht University, in the Netherlands.

Job description

• establish and use mathematical models for large-scale timetabling scheduling, with constraints on vehicles, crew, and infrastructure, able to address placement of buffers

• design and implement a simulation-optimization view to evaluate tentative solutions, considering estimated delay dynamics and possible degrees of rescheduling, to improve proactively and reactively the robustness against small and large delays.

• quantitatively understand the usefulness of the suggested decision, estimate its sensitivity to the considered assumptions; and compared to the typical reaction in real life

Profile

Ideally, you have (or are about to receive) a Masters’ degree in transport sciences, management/ decision sciences, econometrics, mathematics, statistics, computer science, physics or related fields. Your research track is consistent and shows a track record, or clear potential, for analysing, modelling, control, and optimisation of transport systems. You are highly motivated and self-driven, with a clear research vision, academic ambition, and excellent communication and writing skills (fluent spoken and written English is mandatory). Ricercatore medico in ottimizzazione per orari ferroviari robusti 100%, Zurigo, a tempo determinato stampa Druppo Nonostante l'eccellente qualità dei sistemi di trasporto pubblico in Svizzera, il sistema ferroviario deve aumentare le sue prestazioni (qualità, ad esempio, tempi di viaggio e ritardi) e la capacità (importo dei servizi gestiti) e attirare più viaggiatori per soddisfare gli obiettivi ambiziosi da obiettivi politici e ambientali. Un aspetto chiave dei tradizionali sistemi di trasporto ferroviario è il loro piano, che si basa su percorsi predeterminati, linee e tempi programmati, con poca possibilità di adattarsi a circostanze non pianificate e inaspettate. D'altra parte, ritardi e interruzioni potrebbero influenzare molti servizi in tutta una rete per mezzo di propagazione. Il progetto si concentra sulla pianificazione degli orari che è in grado di minimizzare i ritardi e i loro impatti. Per farlo, l'ottimizzazione su larga scala affronta il problema del timetabling ferroviario. In genere vengono utilizzati approcci di programmazione lineare Integer Misti, matematicamente complessi, e con alcuni limiti, quando si modella la complessità della vita reale. Incorporare robustezza contro ritardi è un ulteriore aspetto importante. Questo progetto presuppone che siamo in grado di quantificare come piccoli ritardi si sviluppano e si propagano in tutta la rete; come le interruzioni più grandi si sviluppano e si propagano nella rete. Dato questo, vogliamo determinare orari robusti, con una scelta adeguata di buffer e riserve di tempo di esecuzione. Quei orari, in ritardo, sono in grado di eseguire quantitativamente meglio (cioè meno ritardi, meno ritardi,...). Questa posizione sarà disponibile, con una data di partenza ideale tra agosto 2026 e febbraio 2027, o più avanti d'accordo; la durata prevista del contratto iniziale è di 18 mesi, dopo di che un colloquio attitudinale determinerà l'ulteriore proseguimento del progetto di dottorato. Il progetto di dottorato totale dovrebbe essere terminato in 4 anni in totale. Sfondo del progetto L'obiettivo di questo progetto è quello di capire come gli orari differenti si traducano in dinamiche complesse come risposta ad eventi esterni (piccoli ritardi, interruzioni più grandi). La sfida scientifica consiste nell'integrare quelle dinamiche nei modelli di timetabling esistenti, per identificare gli orari effettivamente migliori, in ritardo. Questa ricerca mira al miglioramento dei modelli di pianificazione degli orari, regolando l'importo e il posizionamento dei buffer e i tempi di riserva. Il progetto è progettato in collaborazione con i player del settore che operano come responsabile delle infrastrutture ferroviarie. Le basi di progetto sui risolutori disponibili per il timetabling non periodico, che includono gli approcci MILP e Logic-Based Benders-Decomposition. Questa ricerca si svolge all'interno di una cooperazione internazionale con il gruppo Complex Systems dell'Università Utrecht, nei Paesi Bassi. Descrizione del lavoro
• stabilire e utilizzare modelli matematici per la pianificazione di tempi di grandi dimensioni, con vincoli su veicoli, equipaggio e infrastrutture, in grado di affrontare il posizionamento dei buffer
• progettare e implementare una visione di simulazione-ottimizzazione per valutare soluzioni tentative, considerando le dinamiche di ritardo stimate e possibili gradi di riprogrammazione, per migliorare proattivamente e reattivamente la robustezza contro piccoli e grandi ritardi.
• comprendere quantitativamente l'utilità della decisione suggerita, valutare la sua sensibilità ai presupposti considerati; e rispetto alla reazione tipica nella vita reale Profilo Idealmente, hai (o stai per ricevere) un master in scienze dei trasporti, scienze della gestione/decisione, econometriche, matematica, statistiche, informatica, fisica o campi correlati. La vostra pista di ricerca è coerente e mostra un track record, o un potenziale chiaro, per analizzare, modellare, controllare e ottimizzare i sistemi di trasporto. Sei altamente motivato e auto-guidato, con una chiara visione di ricerca, ambizione accademica, e eccellenti capacità di comunicazione e scrittura (il fluente parlato e scritto inglese è obbligatorio). Inoltre, sono previste le seguenti competenze

Doktorand in der Optimierung für robuste Bahnfahrpläne 100%, Zürich, befristet Drucken Drucken Trotz der ausgezeichneten Qualität der öffentlichen Verkehrssysteme in der Schweiz muss das Eisenbahnsystem seine Leistungsfähigkeit (z.B. Fahrzeit, Verzögerungen) und Kapazität (die Zahl der Dienstleistungen) erhöhen und Reisende mehr anlocken, um den ambitionierten Zielen von politischen und umweltpolitischen Zielen gerecht zu werden. Ein wesentlicher Aspekt der traditionellen Eisenbahnverkehrssysteme ist ihr Plan, der auf vorgegebenen Strecken, Linien und geplanten Zeiten basiert, mit wenig Möglichkeit, sich auf unplanmäßige und unerwartete Umstände einzustellen. Auf der anderen Seite könnten Verzögerungen und Störungen viele Dienste in einem Netzwerk durch Verbreitung beeinflussen. Das Projekt konzentriert sich auf die Planung von Fahrplänen, die Verzögerungen und deren Auswirkungen minimieren können. Zu diesem Zweck befasst sich die groß angelegte Optimierung mit dem eisenbahnbrechenden Problem. Typischerweise werden gemischte Integer Linear Programming-Ansätze verwendet, die mathematisch komplex sind und mit einigen Grenzen, bei der Modellierung der realen Komplexität. Ein weiterer wichtiger Aspekt ist die Robustheit gegen Verzögerungen. Dieses Projekt geht davon aus, dass wir in der Lage sind, zu quantifizieren, wie sich kleine Verzögerungen im gesamten Netzwerk entwickeln und propagieren; wie sich größere Störungen im Netzwerk entwickeln und propagieren. Dabei wollen wir robuste Zeitpläne mit geeigneter Wahl von Puffern und Laufzeitreserven bestimmen. Diese Zeitpläne können unter Verzögerungen quantitativ besser durchgeführt werden (d.h. weniger Verzögerungen, weniger größere Verzögerungen,...). Diese Position wird verfügbar sein, mit einem idealen Starttermin zwischen August 2026 und Februar 2027, oder weiter nach Vereinbarung; die geplante Dauer des ersten Vertrags beträgt 18 Monate, danach wird ein Eignungskolloquium die weitere Fortsetzung des Promotionsprojekts bestimmen. Das gesamte Promotionsprojekt soll in insgesamt 4 Jahren abgeschlossen werden. Projekt Hintergrund Der Schwerpunkt dieses Projekts ist zu verstehen, wie unterschiedliche Zeitpläne zu komplexen Dynamiken führen, als Reaktion auf externe Ereignisse (kleine Verzögerungen, größere Störungen). Die wissenschaftliche Herausforderung besteht darin, diese Dynamik in bestehende Zeitvertreibsmodelle zu integrieren, um jene Zeitpläne zu identifizieren, die tatsächlich besser sind, unter Verzögerungen. Diese Forschung zielt auf die Verbesserung der Zeitplanplanungsmodelle, die Anpassung der Menge und Platzierung von Puffern und Reservezeiten. Das Projekt ist in Zusammenarbeit mit dem als Eisenbahninfrastrukturmanager tätigen Industrieplayer konzipiert. Das Projekt basiert auf verfügbaren Solvents für nicht-periodische Zeitvertreibungen, darunter MILP und Logic-Based Benders-Decomposition Ansätze. Diese Forschung wird in einer internationalen Zusammenarbeit mit der Gruppe Complex Systems an der Universität Utrecht in den Niederlanden durchgeführt. Jobbeschreibung
• Erstellung und Nutzung von mathematischen Modellen für die umfassende Zeitplanung, mit Einschränkungen für Fahrzeuge, Besatzung und Infrastruktur, in der Lage, die Platzierung von Puffern
• Entwurf und Umsetzung einer Simulationsoptimierungs-Ansicht zur Bewertung von zeltativen Lösungen unter Berücksichtigung der geschätzten Verzögerungsdynamik und der möglichen Umplanungsgrade, um die Robustheit gegenüber kleinen und großen Verzögerungen proaktiv und reaktiv zu verbessern.
• die Nützlichkeit der vorgeschlagenen Entscheidung quantitativ zu verstehen, ihre Empfindlichkeit auf die betrachteten Annahmen zu schätzen; und im Vergleich zur typischen Reaktion im realen Leben Profil Idealerweise haben Sie (oder sind über zu empfangen) einen Master-Abschluss in Transportwissenschaften, Management / Entscheidungswissenschaften, Ökonometrie, Mathematik, Statistik, Informatik, Physik oder verwandten Bereichen. Ihr Forschungspfad ist konsistent und zeigt einen Rekord oder ein klares Potenzial für die Analyse, Modellierung, Steuerung und Optimierung von Transportsystemen. Sie sind hoch motiviert und selbstfahrend, mit einer klaren Forschungsvision, akademischem Ehrgeiz und exzellenten Kommunikations- und Schreibfähigkeiten ( fließendes gesprochenes und geschriebenes Englisch ist obligatorisch). jobs.description:
Teaching and Research Assistant at the Institute of Design and Architecture

40%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

D-ARCH is a leading research and teaching institution dedicated to the advancement of architectural design at the building, urban, landscape and territorial scales. Architectural design is fundamentally holistic in that it utilises a broad epistemological and technical apparatus to give shape to cultural, ecological, environmental, social and economic needs. And, by constitution, architectural design is concerned both with the analysis of the past and the making of the future at every scale, from the local to the global.

Job description

• Assist and be part of the chair team projects

• Provide your technical and architectural expertise

• Prepare & process teaching and research materials

• Assist & supervise students in developing their projects

Profile

• Architect 2/3+ years experience

• Fluent in English and (Swiss) German

• French is valued

• Preferably starting your own practice

• Taste for hands-on work / construction

• Experience in construction is valued

Workplace

Workplace

We offer

• Fixed-term contract (one year, renewable)

• Position start in September 2026

• Work primarily on Tuesdays and Wednesdays

• Your career with impact: Become part of ETH Zurich, which not only supports your professional development, but also actively contributes to positive change in society

• We are actively committed to a sustainable and climate-neutral university

• You can expect numerous benefits , such as public transport season tickets and car sharing, a wide range of sports offered by the ASVZ, childcare and attractive pension benefits

chevron_right
Working, teaching and research at ETH Zurich

We value diversity and sustainability

In line with our values , ETH Zurich encourages an inclusive culture. We promote equality of opportunity, value diversity and nurture a working and learning environment in which the rights and dignity of all our staff and students are respected. Visit our Equal Opportunities and Diversity website to find out how we ensure a fair and open environment that allows everyone to grow and flourish. Sustainability is a core value for us – we are consistently working towards a climate-neutral future .

Curious? So are we.

We look forward to receiving your online application with the following documents in a single PDF (max 10 MB) containing:

• CV (1 page)

• Cover letter (1 page)

• Portfolio

Further information about the Department and the Institute can be found on our website . Questions regarding the position should be directed to application.theriot@arch.ethz.ch (no applications).

Please note that we exclusively accept applications submitted through our online application portal. Applications via email or postal services will not be considered.

About ETH Zürich

ETH Zurich is one of the world’s leading universities specialising in
science and technology. We are renowned for our excellent education,
cutting-edge fundamental research and direct transfer of new knowledge
into society. Over 30,000 people from more than 120 countries find our
university to be a place that promotes independent thinking and an
environment that inspires excellence. Located in the heart of Europe,
yet forging connections all over the world, we work together to
develop solutions for the global challenges of today and tomorrow.

jobs.description:
Doctoral position on PFAS Pathways: Tracking “Forever Chemicals” through Soil–Groundwater Interfaces for Safer Water

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

The Subsurface Environmental Processes Group (Eawag and ETH Zurich) is seeking a dynamic and motivated doctoral student to study the dynamics of PFAS in subsurface environments. Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are a class of highly persistent synthetic compounds increasingly detected in soils and aquifers worldwide. Their extreme stability and mobility make PFAS a critical challenge for groundwater quality and drinking water security. Although PFAS contamination has been reported in many regions, the fundamental mechanisms controlling PFAS fate and transport in coupled soil–aquifer systems remain poorly understood.

Job description

• The focus of this PhD project will be on quantifying the control exerted by soil physico-chemical properties and episodic recharge events on the fate, transport, and transformation of PFAS

• The student will have the unique opportunity to learn, develop, and apply a range of cutting-edge (laboratory) experimental and modeling techniques, including the integration of machine learning and process-based models

• Measurements will be guided by and compared with the modeling developed in this project

• Findings will help advance our knowledge of governing processes of PFAS mobility in soils and aquifers, providing a robust scientific basis for predictive modelling, risk assessment, and the development of sustainable groundwater protection strategies

Profile

• The successful candidate should have a background in groundwater hydrology, soil physics, engineering, or related areas, with a strong quantitative inclination

• They should have a desire to work experimentally at the interface between physics, chemistry, and engineering, and to combine experimental research with mathematical modeling

• The student will have the opportunity to work in a highly interdisciplinary, fast-paced research environment, to gain skills in several technologies (analytical and computational), to learn about fundamental physical and chemical processes in porous media and subsurface environmental processes in general, and to interact with world-class collaborators in environmental chemistry, reactive transport, and hybrid approaches (process-based models and machine learning)

• The ability to work independently, but also to interact and collaborate within a team, will be a great asset

• An interest for contributing to teaching activities is highly valued

• The project will be supervised by Prof. Dr. Joaquin Jimenez-Martinez (Eawag and ETH Zurich)

Workplace

Workplace

We offer

• Your job with impact: Become part of ETH Zurich, which not only supports your professional development, but also actively contributes to positive change in society

• You can expect numerous benefits , such as public transport season tickets and car sharing, a wide range of sports offered by the ASVZ , childcare and attractive pension benefits

We value diversity and sustainability

In line with our values , ETH Zurich encourages an inclusive culture. We promote equality of opportunity, value diversity and nurture a working and learning environment in which the rights and dignity of all our staff and students are respected. Visit our Equal Opportunities and Diversity website to find out how we ensure a fair and open environment that allows everyone to grow and flourish. Sustainability is a core value for us – we are consistently working towards a climate-neutral future .

Curious? So are we.

We look forward to receiving your online application with the following documents:

• a CV

• full transcripts from undergraduate studies (both Bachelor and Masters)

• a brief (1-2 page) statement of research interests

• at least 2 (preferably 3) letters of reference

jobs.description:
Postdoc position in light multiplexed, fiber-based artificial sensorimotor network

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

The Robotic Materials group is looking for a highly motivated postdoc for the topic of light multiplexed artificial sensorimotor network . This position is funded by our ERC Starting Grant .

Project background

The introduction of fiber optics in the 1970s has revolutionized the telecommunications industry upon the replacement of copper wires and played a major role in the advent of the Information Age - One high bandwidth fiber optic cable can replace thousands of electrical links to transmit the same amount of information. As a parallel to the thriving fields of soft devices and robots controlled by electrical signals, soft optics is emerging as a new platform that uses the modulation of light in soft matter to encode multifunctionalities in the optical path.

The focus of this project is to expand both actuation and sensing capacities with light. The project will create an artificial sensorimotor network with densely distributed actuators and sensors similar to the biological neuromasculature. The first part of the project will develop a single soft optical fiber with distributed multimodal actuators that are also self-sensing. The second part will study grouped behavior of these “muscle bundles” to enable muscle coordination for complex/adaptive/efficient movements.

Job description

• Based on existing light actuators in our group, develop self-sensing methods where the transducer serves both for actuation and sensing, and is feedback controlled with onboard optoelectronics

• Design and microfabrication of a soft optical fiber distributed with such transducers configured for multiple modalities, and enable individual addressability through light multiplexing, based on the group’s expertise

• Demonstrate the single artificial neuromuscular fiber for advanced robotic functions arising from the distributed and multimodal actuators and sensors

• In the second part, create grouped neuromuscular bundles with extremely high functional density approaching orders of magnitude of biology

• Investigate emergent coordinated bundle behavior and motion patterns arising from biologically similar redundancy with collaborations of control and learning

• Demonstrate for advanced robotic functions

• Supervise master/bachelor students

• Teaching assistant for the robotic materials class

This is a full-time position that starts as soon as possible. Applications are evaluated on a rolling basis until the position is filled.

Profile

• PhD degree in Robotics, Mechanical Engineering, Materials Science and Engineering or related fields from a top university

• Strong research track records in one or more of the following: micro robots, soft robotics, fiber-based robots, or related

• Hands-on experience in robot design, prototyping, experimental characterization, and TRL 3-5 demonstration

• Knowledge of reconfigurable/multifunctional microrobots, small-scale soft robotics, feedback controlled soft robotic systems is highly desirable

• Excellent problem-solving abilities and a passion for interdisciplinary research

Workplace

Workplace

We offer

• A productive working environment with training and guidance from the PI on a regular basis

• Competitive salary according to ETH standards (fully funded, full-time, fixed term position)

• An interdisciplinary, international, and diverse team of talents and a stimulating, vibrant, collaborative group

• Strong connections with academic, industrial, and clinical partners in materials science, robotics, and healthcare

Questa posizione è finanziata dal nostro ERC Start Grant . Sfondo del progetto L'introduzione di fibre ottiche negli anni '70 ha rivoluzionato l'industria delle telecomunicazioni sulla sostituzione dei fili di rame e ha svolto un ruolo importante nell'avvento dell'età dell'informazione - Un cavo in fibra ottica ad alta larghezza di banda può sostituire migliaia di collegamenti elettrici per trasmettere la stessa quantità di informazioni. Parallelamente ai campi fiorenti di dispositivi morbidi e robot controllati da segnali elettrici, l'ottica morbida sta emergendo come una nuova piattaforma che utilizza la modulazione della luce in materia morbida per codificare le multifunzionalità nel percorso ottico. L'obiettivo di questo progetto è di espandere sia le capacità di azionamento che di rilevamento con la luce. Il progetto creerà una rete di sensorimotori artificiali con attuatori e sensori densamente distribuiti simili alla neuromascolatura biologica. La prima parte del progetto svilupperà una singola fibra ottica morbida con attuatori multimodali distribuiti che sono anche auto-sensibilizzanti. La seconda parte studierà il comportamento raggruppato di questi “pacchetti muscolari” per consentire il coordinamento muscolare per movimenti complessi/adaptivi/efficienti. Descrizione del lavoro • Basato sugli attuatori di luce esistenti nel nostro gruppo, sviluppare metodi di auto-sensazione in cui il trasduttore serve sia per l'azione che per il rilevamento, ed è controllato da feedback con optoelettronica a bordo • Design e microfabricazione di una fibra ottica morbida distribuita con tali trasduttori configurati per molteplici modalità, e consentire l'individual indirizzabilità attraverso il multiplexing della luce, in base alle competenze del gruppo • Dimostrare il singolo neuromus artificiale avanzato Nella seconda parte, creare fasci neuromuscolari raggruppati con densità funzionale estremamente elevata avvicinando ordini di grandezza della biologia • Investigare comportamenti e modelli di movimento coordinati dei fasci emerse derivanti da ridondanza biologicamente simile con collaborazioni di controllo e apprendimento • Dimostrare funzioni robotiche avanzate • Supervise master/bachelor studenti • Assistente didattico per la classe dei materiali robotici Questa è una posizione a tempo pieno che inizia il prima possibile. descriptionByLocale.fr: chevron left Übersicht chevron left Übersicht Postdoc position in light multiplexed, fibre-based artificielle sensorimotor network 100%, Zurich, print à terme fixe Drucken Le groupe Robotic Materials recherche un postdoc très motivé pour le thème du réseau de capteurs artificiels multiplexed light. Ce poste est financé par notre subvention de démarrage du CEE . Contexte du projet L'introduction de la fibre optique dans les années 1970 a révolutionné l'industrie des télécommunications en remplaçant les fils de cuivre et a joué un rôle majeur dans l'avènement de l'ère de l'information - Un câble fibre optique à bande passante élevée peut remplacer des milliers de liaisons électriques pour transmettre la même quantité d'information. Parallèlement aux champs florissants d'appareils et de robots doux commandés par des signaux électriques, l'optique douce apparaît comme une nouvelle plateforme qui utilise la modulation de la lumière en matière douce pour coder les multifonctions dans le chemin optique. Ce projet vise à développer les capacités d'action et de détection avec la lumière. Le projet créera un réseau de capteurs moteurs artificiels avec des actionneurs et des capteurs densément distribués semblables à la neuromasculature biologique. La première partie du projet développera une seule fibre optique douce avec des actionneurs multimodaux distribués qui sont également auto-sensibilisants. La deuxième partie étudiera le comportement groupé de ces faisceaux musculaires afin de permettre la coordination musculaire pour des mouvements complexes, adaptés et efficaces. jobs.description:
Postdoc position in soft optical fiber-based artificial muscle for biomedical applications

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

The Robotic Materials group is looking for a highly motivated postdoc for the topic of soft optical fiber-based artificial muscle for biomedical applications . This position is funded by our ERC Starting Grant .

Project background

The introduction of fiber optics in the 1970s has revolutionized the telecommunications industry upon the replacement of copper wires and played a major role in the advent of the Information Age - One high bandwidth fiber optic cable can replace thousands of electrical links to transmit the same amount of information. As a parallel to the thriving fields of soft devices and robots controlled by electrical signals, soft optics is emerging as a new platform that uses the modulation of light in soft matter to encode multifunctionalities in the optical path.

The focus of this project is to create biocompatible, high performance soft actuators multiplexed by light, all integrated on a miniature fiber, delivering advanced robotic and biomedical functions as minimally invasive surgical tools and implantable devices.

Job description

• Develop biocompatible soft actuators controlled by light with performance matching benchmarked soft robotic actuators

• Design and microfabrication of soft optical fibers densely distributed with actuators

• Develop actuator multiplexing methods for individual addressability

• Demonstration for advanced robotic functions as minimally invasive surgical tools

• Integration with bioelectronic functions (e.g., sensing) for closed-loop controlled diagnostic and therapeutic functions.

• Demonstration as robotic/biomedical devices for real-world application through collaborations.

• Supervise master/bachelor students

• Teaching assistant for the robotic materials class

Profile

• PhD degree in Materials Science and Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or related fields from a top university.

• Strong research track records in one or more of the following: bioelectronics, soft robotics, flexible electronics, fiber-based devices, functional materials, wearable systems, or biomedical devices.

• Hands-on experience in device design, prototyping, experimental characterization, and TRL 3-5 demonstrations.

• Knowledge of biomedical soft materials, textile/fiber processing, microfabrication, or soft actuators is highly desirable

• Excellent problem-solving abilities and a passion for interdisciplinary research.

Workplace

Workplace

We offer

• A productive working environment with training and guidance from the PI on a regular basis

• Competitive salary according to ETH standards (fully funded, full-time, fixed term position)

• An interdisciplinary, international, and diverse team of talents and a stimulating, vibrant, collaborative group

• Strong connections with academic, industrial, and clinical partners in materials science, robotics, and healthcare.

chevron_right
Working, teaching and research at ETH Zurich

We value diversity and sustainability

In line with our values , ETH Zurich encourages an inclusive culture. We promote equality of opportunity, value diversity and nurture a working and learning environment in which the rights and dignity of all our staff and students are respected. Visit our Equal Opportunities and Diversity website to find out how we ensure a fair and open environment that allows everyone to grow and flourish. Sustainability is a core value for us – we are consistently working towards a climate-neutral future .

Curious? So are we.

• A cover letter

• CV

• Publication list with a few sentences highlighting representative works

• Contact details of two referees

• Optional: transcripts of academic records

The preferred start date is as soon as possible in the third quarter of 2026 .

The Robotic Materials group is looking for a highly motivated PhD student for the topic of light programmable stiffness for reconfigurable soft devices and robots. This 4-year PhD position is funded by our ERC Starting Grant .

Project background

The introduction of fiber optics in the 1970s has revolutionized the telecommunications industry upon the replacement of copper wires and played a major role in the advent of the Information Age - One high bandwidth fiber optic cable can replace thousands of electrical links to transmit the same amount of information. descriptionByLocale.en: PhD position in light controlled variable stiffness for soft robotics 100%, Zurich, fixed-term print Drucken The Robotic Materials group is looking for a highly motivated PhD student for the topic of light programmable stiffness for reconfigurable soft devices and robots. This 4-year PhD position is funded by our ERC Starting Grant . Project background The introduction of fiber optics in the 1970s has revolutionized the telecommunications industry upon the replacement of copper wires and played a major role in the advent of the Information Age - One high bandwidth fiber optic cable can replace thousands of electrical links to transmit the same amount of information. As a parallel to the thriving fields of soft devices and robots controlled by electrical signals, soft optics is emerging as a new platform that uses the modulation of light in soft matter to encode multifunctionalities in the optical path. The first part of this project will center around developing light-stimulated stiffness programming methods that surpass the performance of current variable stiffness benchmarks. The second part will focus on the application of this principle in several soft device/robot systems to demonstrate reconfigurability and multifunctionality for real-world tasks. jobs.description:
Postdoc Position in Experimental Quantum Engineering (EQE) Group

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

The Experimental Quantum Engineering (EQE) group at ETH Zurich and the Paul Scherrer Institute (PSI) invites applications for a highly motivated postdoctoral researcher to work at the interface of quantum optics, quantum information science and quantum many-body physics.

Led by Prof. Wenchao Xu , the EQE group develops programmable quantum systems based on neutral atoms and Rydberg interactions to advance both fundamental quantum science and next-generation quantum technologies. Our research combines atomic physics, quantum control, and scalable architectures for fault-tolerant quantum computation, hybrid quantum simulation, and quantum-enhanced sensing.

Project background

Our group addresses key challenges in quantum science by building and exploiting hybrid quantum systems consisting of individually controlled atoms and atomic ensembles.

Current research directions include:

• Demonstrating scalable architectures for fault-tolerant quantum information processing, featuring reconfigurable local control, rapid quantum non-demolition readout, and fast error-syndrome extraction

• Developing strong atom–light interfaces to enable quantum interconnects and modular quantum systems

• Investigating non-equilibrium quantum many-body dynamics and quantum information dynamics in programmable atom arrays

Job description

We seek a postdoctoral researcher to contribute to a new experimental platform based on dual-type tweezer atom arrays.

The project aims to demonstrate the unique advantages for:

• Reconfigurable local quantum control

• Rapid, non-demolition state detection of both single- and multi-qubit states

• Novel phenomena in quantum dynamics arising from the interplay with measurement

These capabilities enable new routes toward fault-tolerant quantum computation and open exciting opportunities for exploring frontier problems in quantum information dynamics.

The successful candidate will:

• Design, build, and operate state-of-the-art neutral-atom experiments

• Demonstrate novel quantum control and measurement protocols

• Lead research projects and mentor students

• Collaborate closely with researchers at ETH Zurich, PSI, and international partners

More information about the project and the group can be found on our website .

Starting date: flexible in 2026

Employment: full-time

Profile

• PhD in physics or a related field

• Strong background in experimental AMO physics or quantum optics

• Experience with cold atoms, optical tweezers, lasers, or quantum control techniques is highly desirable

• Strong interest in neutral-atom quantum technologies and many-body quantum physics

• Ability to work both independently and collaboratively

• Good communication skills in English (German is a plus)

Workplace

Workplace

We offer

• A highly creative and collaborative research environment

• Freedom to develop independent research directions

• Access to world-class infrastructure at ETH Zurich and PSI

• Opportunities for interdisciplinary and international collaborations

• Competitive salary and benefits

chevron_right
Working, teaching and research at ETH Zurich

We value diversity and sustainability

In line with our values , ETH Zurich encourages an inclusive culture. We promote equality of opportunity, value diversity and nurture a working and learning environment in which the rights and dignity of all our staff and students are respected. Visit our Equal Opportunities and Diversity website to find out how we ensure a fair and open environment that allows everyone to grow and flourish. Sustainability is a core value for us – we are consistently working towards a climate-neutral future .

Curious? So are we.

We look forward to receiving your online application with the following documents:

• CV (with publication list)

• Cover letter

• 2-3 references

Please submit your application through our onli

descriptionByLocale.de: Beschreibung Postdoc Position in Experimental Quantum Engineering (EQE) Gruppe 100%, Zürich, befristet Drucken Drucken Die Gruppe Experimental Quantum Engineering (EQE) der ETH Zürich und des Paul Scherrer Institute (PSI) lädt Applikationen für einen hochmotivierten Postdoc-Forscher ein, an der Schnittstelle von Quantenoptik, Quanteninformationswissenschaft und Quantenvielkörperphysik zu arbeiten. Unter der Leitung von Prof. Wenchao Xu entwickelt die EQE-Gruppe programmierbare Quantensysteme auf Basis neutraler Atome und Rydberg-Interaktionen, um sowohl grundlegende Quantenwissenschaft als auch Quantentechnologien der nächsten Generation voranzutreiben. Unsere Forschung kombiniert Atomphysik, Quantenkontrolle und skalierbare Architekturen für fehlertolerante Quantenberechnung, Hybrid-Quantensimulation und quantenverstärkte Erfassung. Projekt Hintergrund Unsere Gruppe beschäftigt sich mit den wichtigsten Herausforderungen in der Quantenwissenschaft, indem sie Hybrid-Quantensysteme aus individuell kontrollierten Atomen und Atomensembles baut und nutzt. Aktuelle Forschungsrichtungen umfassen: • Demonstration skalierbarer Architekturen für die fehlertolerante Quanteninformationsverarbeitung, mit rekonfigurierbarer lokaler Kontrolle, schnellem Quanten-nicht-Demolitions-Auslesen und schneller Fehler-Syndrome-Extraktion • Entwicklung starker Atom-Licht-Schnittstellen, um Quanten-Verbindungen und modulare Quantensysteme zu ermöglichen • Untersuchung von Nicht-Equilibrium-Quanten-Malkörperdynamik und Quanteninformationsdynamik in programmierbaren Atomarrays Jobbeschreibung Wir suchen einen Postdoc-Forscher, um zu einer neuen experimentellen Plattform auf Basis von Dual-Typ-Tweezer-Atom-Arrays beizutragen. descriptionByLocale.fr: Descrizione Position postdoc dans le groupe d'ingénierie quantique expérimentale (EQE) 100%, Zurich, durée déterminée imprimer Drucken Le groupe Experimental Quantum Engineering (EQE) de l'ETH Zurich et l'Institut Paul Scherrer (PSI) invitent un chercheur postdoctoral hautement motivé à travailler à l'interface de l'optique quantique, de la science de l'information quantique et de la physique quantique de nombreux corps. jobs.description:
Systems Engineer – Cloud and Platform Services

80%-100%, Lugano, fixed-term

print
Drucken

The Swiss National Supercomputing Centre (CSCS) develops and operates a high-performance computing and data research infrastructure that supports world-class science in Switzerland. Its user laboratory is available to domestic and international researchers in academia, industry, and the business sector. The centre is operated by ETH Zurich and has offices at its data centre in Lugano and in Zurich.

Project background

As high-performance computing, AI, and cloud technologies continue to converge, CSCS is redefining how to design and deliver advanced computational services. Modern scientific and engineering workloads are no longer just large; they are complex, data-intensive, and highly diverse, meaning they push existing infrastructure to its limits.

This position is funded via the Helvetic AI Resources ,Technologies, and Services (HEARTS) project, and is based on a two‑year contract, which can be extended or potentially become permanent.

Our core values:

We are looking for candidates who share our guiding principles:

• Curiosity: You enjoy learning, exploring new ideas, and understanding problems deeply.

• Openness: You listen, collaborate, and are receptive to different perspectives.

• Courage: You take responsibility and tackle challenging or ambiguous problems. You are willing to take initiative and have the difficult conversations that can move a team forward.

• Supportive: You help colleagues and users succeed and contribute to a positive team culture.

• Integrity: You act honestly, ethically, and reliably. and take ownership of your work.

Job description

• The primary goal of this position is to design, implement, and operate scalable inference services within a multi-tenant HPC infrastructure

• As a systems engineer, you will play a key role in the architecture deployment, operation, and documentation of production-grade inference platforms that support a wide range of AI-driven workloads

Your work will directly influence the evolution of CSCS’s AI and HPC capabilities, which will improve the performance, reliability, and efficiency of our inference services and enable researchers and engineers to deploy and run advanced models at scale.

Profile

You should have a bachelor’s degree or higher in computer engineering, computer science, a relevant technical field, or equivalent practical experience.

You should have a sound knowledge of:

• Linux administration skills

• Deploying services on Kubernetes

• Infrastructure-as-code tools (e.g. Terraform/openTofu)

• Automation tools and framework, including CI/CD processes and ecosystem (e.g., Gitlab CI, HashiCorp Vault)

Experience with the following is preferred, though there will be ample opportunities to learn and gain more experience with all of these skills on the job:

• Versioning systems and CI/CD workflows such as ArgoCD,

• Automated installation systems for physical servers, such as MAAS or Foreman,

• Developing Ansible configurations,

• Developing services on top of Kubernetes.

Personal qualities:

• Self-motivated and proactive team player

• Strong communication skills or interest in developing them

• Strong problem-solving mindset with tolerance for uncertainty and change

• Understands user needs and works collaboratively to address them

• Adaptive and willing to learn new technologies with and from others

• Comfortable tackling complex or ambiguous problems

• Comfortable admitting when you don’t know, reaching out and leveraging the right expertise when needed

Project management and methodology:

• Experience with working in self-organized teams

• Familiarity with Agile methodology

• Experience with test-driven development is a plus

Workplace

Workplace

We offer

• Your job with impact: Become part of ETH Zurich, which not only supports your professional development, but also actively contributes to positive change in soci

descriptionByLocale.it: Ingegnere Sistemi – Servizi Cloud e Piattaforma 80%-100%, Lugano, a tempo determinato stampa Druppo Descrizione Lo Swiss National Supercomputing Centre (CSCS) sviluppa e gestisce un'infrastruttura di calcolo e di ricerca dati ad alte prestazioni che supporta la scienza di livello mondiale in Svizzera. Il suo laboratorio di utenti è disponibile per i ricercatori nazionali e internazionali in accademia, industria e settore business. Il centro è gestito da ETH Zurich e ha sede presso il suo data center di Lugano e a Zurigo. Sfondo del progetto Poiché le tecnologie di calcolo ad alte prestazioni, AI e cloud continuano a convergere, CSCS sta ridefinindo come progettare e fornire servizi computazionali avanzati. I moderni carichi di lavoro scientifici e ingegneristici non sono più solo grandi; sono complessi, intensivi di dati e molto diversi, il che significa che spingono le infrastrutture esistenti ai suoi limiti. Questa posizione è finanziata tramite il progetto Helvetic AI Resources ,Technologies e Services (HEARTS), e si basa su un contratto di due anni, che può essere esteso o potenzialmente diventare permanente. I nostri valori fondamentali Stiamo cercando candidati che condividono i nostri principi guida: • Curiosità: Ti piace imparare, esplorare nuove idee e comprendere i problemi profondamente. • Apertura: Ascolti, collabora e ricettivi a diverse prospettive. • Coraggio: si assume la responsabilità e affrontare problemi impegnativi o ambigui. Siete disposti a prendere l'iniziativa e avere le conversazioni difficili che possono portare avanti una squadra. • Supportive: aiuta i colleghi e gli utenti ad avere successo e a contribuire ad una cultura positiva del team. • Integrità: Lei agisce onestamente, eticamente e in modo affidabile. e prendere la proprietà del vostro lavoro. Descrizione del lavoro • L'obiettivo primario di questa posizione è quello di progettare, implementare e gestire servizi di inferenza scalabile all'interno di un'infrastruttura HPC multi-tenant • In qualità di ingegnere di sistemi, svolgerai un ruolo chiave nella distribuzione dell'architettura, nel funzionamento e nella documentazione delle piattaforme di inferenza di livello di produzione che supportano una vasta gamma di carichi di lavoro basati su AI Il vostro lavoro influenzerà direttamente l'evoluzione delle capacità AI e HPC di CSCS, che miglioreranno le prestazioni, l'affidabilità e l'efficienza dei nostri servizi di inferenza e consentiranno ai ricercatori e agli ingegneri di implementare e gestire modelli avanzati in scala. Profilo Si dovrebbe avere una laurea o superiore in ingegneria informatica, informatica, un campo tecnico rilevante, o esperienza pratica equivalente. Si dovrebbe avere una solida conoscenza di: • competenze di amministrazione Linux • Servizi di distribuzione su Kubernetes • Strumenti di infrastruttura-come-codice (ad esempio Terraform/openTofu) • Strumenti di automazione e framework, inclusi i processi CI/CD e l'ecosistema (ad esempio, Gitlab CI, HashiCorp Vault) L'esperienza con il seguente è preferita, anche se ci saranno ampie opportunità per imparare e acquisire più esperienza con tutte queste competenze sul lavoro: • Sistemi di versione e flussi di lavoro CI/CD come ArgoCD, • Sistemi di installazione automatizzati per server fisici, come MAAS o Foreman, • Sviluppare configurazioni Ansible, • Sviluppo di servizi in cima a Kubernetes. Qualità personali • Giocatore di squadra automotivato e proattivo • Forte capacità di comunicazione o interesse a svilupparle • Forte mentalità problem solving con tolleranza per l'incertezza e il cambiamento • Comprende le esigenze degli utenti e lavora in collaborazione per affrontarli • Adattativo e disposto ad imparare nuove tecnologie con e da altri • Confortevoli problemi complessi o ambigui • Confortevole ammettere quando non si sa, raggiungere e sfruttare la giusta esperienza quando necessario Gestione e metodologia del progetto • Esperienza con il lavoro in team auto-organizzati • Familiarità con la metodologia Agile • L'esperienza con lo sviluppo guidato da test è un plus Luogo di lavoro Luogo di lavoro Cosa? • Il tuo lavoro con impatto: Diventa parte dell'ETH di Zurigo, che non solo supporta lo sviluppo professionale, ma contribuisce attivamente al cambiamento positivo nella società

descriptionByLocale.fr: Ingénieur Systèmes – Services Cloud et Plateforme 80%-100%, Lugano, durée déterminée imprimer Drucken Descrizione Le Centre National de SuperComputation Suisse (CSCS) développe et exploite une infrastructure informatique et de recherche de données de haute performance qui soutient les sciences de classe mondiale en Suisse. Son laboratoire d'utilisateurs est à la disposition des chercheurs canadiens et internationaux du milieu universitaire, de l'industrie et des entreprises. Le centre est exploité par ETH Zurich et dispose de bureaux dans son centre de données à Lugano et à Zurich. Contexte du projet À mesure que les technologies de l'informatique, de l'intelligence artificielle et du cloud continuent de converger, le SCCS redéfinit la façon de concevoir et de fournir des services informatiques avancés. Les charges de travail scientifiques et techniques modernes ne sont plus seulement importantes; elles sont complexes, à forte intensité de données et très diverses, ce qui signifie qu'elles poussent l'infrastructure existante à ses limites. Ce poste est financé par le projet Helvetic AI Resources ,Technologies et Services (HEARTS) et repose sur un contrat de deux ans, qui peut être prolongé ou devenir permanent. Nos valeurs fondamentales Nous cherchons des candidats qui partagent nos principes directeurs : • Curiosité: Vous aimez apprendre, explorer de nouvelles idées et comprendre les problèmes profondément. • Ouverture: Vous écoutez, collaborez et êtes réceptif à différentes perspectives. • Courage: Vous prenez des responsabilités et vous attaquez à des problèmes difficiles ou ambigus. Vous êtes prêt à prendre des initiatives et à avoir les conversations difficiles qui peuvent faire avancer une équipe. • Supportive: Vous aidez vos collègues et utilisateurs à réussir et contribuez à une culture d'équipe positive. • Intégrité : Vous agissez honnêtement, éthiquement et de manière fiable. et prendre en main votre travail. Profil Vous devriez avoir un baccalauréat ou plus en ingénierie informatique, informatique, un domaine technique pertinent, ou une expérience pratique équivalente. Vous devriez avoir une bonne connaissance de: • Compétences en administration Linux • Déploiement de services sur Kubernetes • Outils d'infrastructure comme code (par exemple Terraform/openTofu) • Outils et cadre d'automatisation, y compris les processus CI/CD et l'écosystème (par exemple Gitlab CI, HashiCorp Vault) On préfère l'expérience suivante, bien qu'il y ait de nombreuses possibilités d'apprendre et d'acquérir plus d'expérience avec toutes ces compétences au travail : • Systèmes de version et flux de travail CI/CD tels qu'ArgoCD, • Systèmes d'installation automatisés pour serveurs physiques, tels que MAAS ou Foreman, • Développement de configurations Ansibles, • Développement de services sur Kubernetes. jobs.description:
Doctoral student position – Evaluating novel mineral sources for treatment of micronutrient deficiencies in humans

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

The ETH Zurich Laboratory of Epigenetics, Nutrition and Metabolism and Sustainable Food Processing Group in the Department of Health Science and Technology are running a joint strategic research line on Microalgae and plant-based foods in Human Nutrition and Health . The Sustainable Food Processing group focuses on a system-oriented approach in food production via the consideration of the total value chain, including emerging needs in society and their environmental, economic, and social impact. Innovative raw materials are utilized within urban farming and processing concepts to enable new ways of sustainable food supply. The Laboratory of Epigenetics, Nutrition and Metabolism aims to gain insights into the complex relationship between nutrition, metabolism and the epigenome with advanced techniques such as single-cell and next-generation sequencing techniques as well as human and murine in vivo and in vitro studies and combine these with genome-wide computational and bioinformatic analysis. With strong support from these two ETH groups, we are recruiting as soon as possible a talented and highly motivated doctoral student on the topic of ‘Novel sources of minerals for treatment of micronutrient deficiencies in humans’, focusing on investigating the absorption and bioavailability of novel mineral sources in vivo in clinical trials.

Project background

Micronutrient deficiency is a widespread global health problem, primarily driven by inadequate dietary intake. More than 5 billion people are estimated to not consume enough of at least one micronutrient. Among those, mineral deficiencies can be particularly critical, namely, iron, calcium, zinc, and magnesium deficiencies, which are particularly common in low- and middle-income countries due to low-mineral diets and primarily affect women and children.

Dietary minerals are typically obtained from a variety of foods including animal-based products such as meat, dairy, and seafood, and plant-based foods such as legumes, cereals, nuts, seeds, and leafy vegetables. However, reliance on conventional animal-based foods raises concerns related to environmental sustainability, ethical considerations, and dietary preferences. Although plant-based foods are generally more sustainable, they often have lower mineral content, bioaccessibility, as well as bioavailability due to the presence of absorption inhibitors such as phytates and polyphenols. Given these limitations, the need exists to explore alternative, more sustainable, and mineral-dense food sources that can effectively address global mineral deficiencies.

Novel mineral sources, such as microalgae, could be a rich source of essential minerals, including iron, calcium, zinc, and magnesium, along with proteins, lipids, vitamins, and other bioactive compounds. However, the bioavailability of these minerals needs to be assessed with in vivo clinical trials before large scale application in humans.

Job description

As a doctoral student, you will be responsible for research working towards exploring the absorption and bioavailability of novel mineral sources with clinical trials.

• Summarize the existing knowledge on minerals from novel sources for human nutrition and health

• Design intervention meals (including sensory test) for clinical trials

• Assess the bioaccessibility of minerals in vitro

• Evaluate the mineral bioavailability in vitro

• Carry out clinical trials related to human nutrition enriched with novel mineral sources (key)

• Support teaching activities and co-supervise MSc and BSc students

• Act at the interface between science and technology when supervising students and collaborating with partners from academia and industry

• Support grant applications for the team and support related activities from Singapore-ETH Centre, Bezos Centre for S

descriptionByLocale.it: Descrizione Posizione dottorale degli studenti – Valutazione di nuove fonti minerali per il trattamento delle carenze micronutrienti negli esseri umani 100%, Zurigo, a tempo determinato stampa Druppo Il Laboratorio ETH di Epigenetica, Nutrizione e Metabolismo e Gruppo di Elaborazione Alimentare Sostenibile presso il Dipartimento di Scienze e Tecnologie della Salute gestisce una linea di ricerca strategica congiunta su Microalgae e alimenti a base vegetale nella Nutrizione Umana e nella Salute. Il gruppo Sustainable Food Processing si concentra su un approccio orientato al sistema nella produzione alimentare attraverso la considerazione della catena del valore totale, compresi i bisogni emergenti nella società e il loro impatto ambientale, economico e sociale. Le materie prime innovative sono utilizzate all'interno di concetti di agricoltura urbana e di lavorazione per consentire nuove modalità di approvvigionamento alimentare sostenibile. Il Laboratorio di Epigenetica, Nutrizione e Metabolismo si propone di approfondire il complesso rapporto tra nutrizione, metabolismo e epigeno con tecniche avanzate come le tecniche di sequenziamento monocellulare e di prossima generazione, nonché studi umani e murini in vivo e in vitro e combinarli con l'analisi computazionale e bioinformatica a livello genoma. Con il forte sostegno di questi due gruppi ETH, stiamo reclutando il più presto possibile uno studente di dottorato di talento e altamente motivato sul tema “Novel fonti di minerali per il trattamento delle carenze micronutrienti nell’uomo”, concentrandosi sull’indagine sull’assorbimento e la biodisponibilità di nuove fonti minerali in vivo in studi clinici. Sfondo del progetto La carenza di micronutrienti è un problema di salute globale diffuso, principalmente guidato da un'assunzione dietetica insufficiente. Più di 5 miliardi di persone sono stimate di non consumare abbastanza di almeno un micronutriente. Tra questi, le carenze minerali possono essere particolarmente critiche, vale a dire, le carenze di ferro, calcio, zinco e magnesio, che sono particolarmente comuni nei paesi a basso e medio reddito a causa di diete poco minerali e riguardano principalmente donne e bambini. I minerali alimentari sono tipicamente ottenuti da una varietà di alimenti tra cui prodotti a base di animali come carne, latticini e frutti di mare, e alimenti a base vegetale come legumi, cereali, noci, semi e verdure a foglia. Tuttavia, l'affidamento sugli alimenti tradizionali basati sugli animali solleva preoccupazioni relative alla sostenibilità ambientale, considerazioni etiche e preferenze alimentari. Anche se gli alimenti a base vegetale sono generalmente più sostenibili, hanno spesso contenuti minerali più bassi, bioaccessibilità, così come la biodisponibilità a causa della presenza di inibitori di assorbimento come i fiati e i polifenoli. Data queste limitazioni, esiste la necessità di esplorare fonti alimentari alternative, più sostenibili e minerali che possano affrontare efficacemente le carenze minerali globali. Fonti minerali novelli, come le microalghe, potrebbero essere una ricca fonte di minerali essenziali, tra cui ferro, calcio, zinco e magnesio, insieme a proteine, lipidi, vitamine e altri composti bioattivi. Tuttavia, la biodisponibilità di questi minerali deve essere valutata con studi clinici in vivo prima dell'applicazione su larga scala negli esseri umani. Descrizione del lavoro In qualità di studente di dottorato, sarai responsabile della ricerca che lavorerà per esplorare l'assorbimento e la biodisponibilità di nuove fonti minerali con studi clinici. - Summarizzare le conoscenze esistenti sui minerali da fonti nuove per la nutrizione umana e la salute - Pasti di intervento di progettazione (compreso test sensoriale) per studi clinici - Valutare la bioaccessibilità dei minerali in vitro - Valutare la biodisponibilità minerale in vitro - Effettuare prove cliniche relative alla nutrizione umana arricchita da nuove fonti minerali (chiave) - Supportare attività didattiche e co-supervise studenti MSc e BSc - Agire nell'interfaccia tra scienza e tecnologia quando supervisionare gli studenti e collaborare con i partner dell'accademia e dell'industria - Sostegno alle domande di sovvenzione per il team e le attività di supporto da Singapore-ETH Centre, Bezos Centre for S

descriptionByLocale.de: Beschreibung Doktorandenposition – Bewertung neuartiger Mineralquellen zur Behandlung von Mikronährstoffmangel beim Menschen 100%, Zürich, befristet Drucken Drucken Das ETH Zürich Laboratory of Epigenetics, Nutrition and Metabolism and Sustainable Food Processing Group im Department of Health Science and Technology betreibt eine gemeinsame strategische Forschungslinie über Mikroalgen und pflanzliche Lebensmittel in Human Nutrition and Health. Die Gruppe Sustainable Food Processing konzentriert sich auf einen systemorientierten Ansatz in der Lebensmittelproduktion unter Berücksichtigung der gesamten Wertschöpfungskette, einschließlich der aufstrebenden Bedürfnisse in der Gesellschaft und ihrer ökologischen, wirtschaftlichen und sozialen Auswirkungen. Innovative Rohstoffe werden in städtischen Landwirtschafts- und Verarbeitungskonzepten eingesetzt, um neue Wege der nachhaltigen Lebensmittelversorgung zu ermöglichen. Das Labor für Epigenetik, Ernährung und Metabolismus zielt darauf ab, Einblicke in die komplexe Beziehung zwischen Ernährung, Stoffwechsel und Epigenom mit fortschrittlichen Techniken wie Einzell- und Next-Generation Sequenzierungstechniken sowie menschliche und murine in vivo und in vitro Studien zu gewinnen und diese mit genomweiten rechnerischen und bioinformatischen Analysen zu kombinieren. Mit starker Unterstützung dieser beiden ETH-Gruppen rekrutieren wir so bald wie möglich einen talentierten und hochmotivierten Doktoranden zum Thema „Neue Mineralquellen zur Behandlung von Mikronährstoffmangel beim Menschen“, der sich auf die Untersuchung der Absorption und Bioverfügbarkeit neuartiger Mineralquellen in vivo in klinischen Studien konzentriert. Projekt Hintergrund Mikronährstoffmangel ist ein weit verbreitetes globales Gesundheitsproblem, vor allem durch unzureichende Nahrungsaufnahme angetrieben. Mehr als 5 Milliarden Menschen werden geschätzt, um nicht genug von mindestens einem Mikronährstoff zu konsumieren. Unter diesen können mineralische Mängel besonders kritisch sein, nämlich Eisen-, Kalzium-, Zink- und Magnesiummangel, die besonders häufig in Ländern mit niedrigem und mittlerem Einkommen aufgrund niedrigmineralischer Ernährung und vor allem Frauen und Kinder betreffen. Dietäre Mineralien werden typischerweise aus einer Vielzahl von Lebensmitteln wie Fleisch, Milch und Meeresfrüchten sowie pflanzlichen Lebensmitteln wie Hülsenfrüchten, Getreide, Nüssen, Samen und fruchtigen Gemüsen gewonnen. Die Abhängigkeit von konventionellen tierbasierten Lebensmitteln führt jedoch zu Bedenken im Zusammenhang mit ökologischer Nachhaltigkeit, ethischen Erwägungen und Ernährungspräferenzen. Obwohl pflanzliche Lebensmittel in der Regel nachhaltiger sind, haben sie aufgrund der Anwesenheit von Absorptionsinhibitoren wie Phytate und Polyphenole oft einen geringeren Mineralgehalt, eine Bioverfügbarkeit sowie eine Bioverfügbarkeit. Angesichts dieser Einschränkungen besteht die Notwendigkeit, alternative, nachhaltigere und mineraldichte Lebensmittelquellen zu erforschen, die weltweite Mineralmangel wirksam beheben können. Neuartige Mineralquellen wie Mikroalgen könnten eine reiche Quelle von essentiellen Mineralien sein, einschließlich Eisen, Calcium, Zink und Magnesium, zusammen mit Proteinen, Lipiden, Vitaminen und anderen bioaktiven Verbindungen. Die Bioverfügbarkeit dieser Minerale muss jedoch vor der großtechnischen Anwendung im Menschen mit in vivo klinischen Studien beurteilt werden. Jobbeschreibung Als Doktorandin sind Sie für die Forschung verantwortlich, um die Absorption und Bioverfügbarkeit neuartiger Mineralquellen mit klinischen Studien zu erforschen. - Verbessern Sie das vorhandene Wissen über Mineralien aus neuartigen Quellen für die menschliche Ernährung und Gesundheit - Design Interventionsmehle (einschließlich sensorischer Test) für klinische Studien - Ermöglicht die biologische Zugänglichkeit von Mineralien in vitro - Bewertung der Mineralbioverfügbarkeit in vitro - Durchführung klinischer Studien im Zusammenhang mit der menschlichen Ernährung mit neuartigen Mineralquellen (Schlüssel) - UnterstÃ1⁄4tzung von Lehraktivitäten und Co-Supervise MSc und BSc Studenten - Akt an der Schnittstelle zwischen Wissenschaft und Technologie bei der Betreuung von Studenten und Zusammenarbeit mit Partnern aus Wissenschaft und Industrie - Unterstützungsanträge für das Team und unterstützende Aktivitäten des Singapore-ETH Centre, Bezos Centre for S
descriptionByLocale.fr: Descrizione Position des étudiants au doctorat – Évaluation de nouvelles sources minérales pour le traitement des carences en micronutriments chez l'homme 100%, Zurich, durée déterminée imprimer Drucken Le Laboratoire d'épigénétique, de nutrition et de métabolisme et le Groupe de la transformation durable des aliments du Département de la science et de la technologie de la santé de Zurich gèrent une ligne de recherche stratégique conjointe sur les microalgues et les aliments à base de plantes dans la nutrition et la santé humaines. Le groupe de la transformation durable des aliments se concentre sur une approche systémique de la production alimentaire en tenant compte de la chaîne de valeur totale, y compris les besoins émergents de la société et leurs incidences environnementales, économiques et sociales. Les matières premières innovantes sont utilisées dans l'agriculture urbaine et les concepts de transformation pour permettre de nouveaux modes d'approvisionnement alimentaire durable. Le Laboratoire d'Epigénétique, de Nutrition et de Métabolisme vise à mieux comprendre la relation complexe entre la nutrition, le métabolisme et l'épigénome avec des techniques avancées telles que les techniques de séquençage monocellulaire et de prochaine génération, ainsi que les études in vivo et in vitro humaines et murines, et à les combiner avec des analyses computationnelles et bio-informatiques à l'échelle du génome. Avec l'appui fort de ces deux groupes d'ETH, nous recrutons dès que possible un doctorant talentueux et très motivé sur le thème «Nouvelles sources de minéraux pour le traitement des carences en micronutriments chez l'humain», en se concentrant sur l'étude de l'absorption et de la biodisponibilité de nouvelles sources minérales in vivo dans les essais cliniques. Contexte du projet La carence en micronutriments est un problème de santé mondial généralisé, principalement dû à une alimentation inadéquate. On estime que plus de 5 milliards de personnes ne consomment pas suffisamment d'au moins un micronutriment. Parmi celles-ci, les carences minérales peuvent être particulièrement critiques, à savoir les carences en fer, en calcium, en zinc et en magnésium, qui sont particulièrement courantes dans les pays à faible revenu et à revenu intermédiaire en raison de régimes à faible revenu minier et touchent principalement les femmes et les enfants. Les minéraux alimentaires sont généralement obtenus à partir de divers aliments, notamment des produits à base d'animaux comme la viande, les produits laitiers et les fruits de mer, et des aliments à base de plantes comme les légumineuses, les céréales, les noix, les graines et les légumes à feuilles. Toutefois, la dépendance à l'égard des aliments traditionnels à base d'animaux soulève des préoccupations liées à la durabilité environnementale, aux considérations éthiques et aux préférences alimentaires. Bien que les aliments à base de plantes soient généralement plus durables, ils ont souvent une teneur minérale inférieure, la bioaccessibilité, ainsi que la biodisponibilité en raison de la présence d'inhibiteurs d'absorption tels que les phytates et les polyphénols. Compte tenu de ces limites, il est nécessaire d'explorer d'autres sources alimentaires, plus durables et plus riches en minéraux, susceptibles de remédier efficacement aux carences minérales mondiales. De nouvelles sources minérales, comme les microalgues, pourraient être une riche source de minéraux essentiels, notamment le fer, le calcium, le zinc et le magnésium, ainsi que des protéines, des lipides, des vitamines et d'autres composés bioactifs. Cependant, la biodisponibilité de ces minéraux doit être évaluée au moyen d'essais cliniques in vivo avant une application à grande échelle chez l' homme. Description du poste En tant qu'étudiant au doctorat, vous serez responsable de la recherche visant à explorer l'absorption et la biodisponibilité de nouvelles sources minérales avec des essais cliniques. - Résumer les connaissances existantes sur les minéraux provenant de sources nouvelles pour la nutrition et la santé humaines - Concevoir des repas d'intervention (y compris des tests sensoriels) pour les essais cliniques - Évaluer la bioaccessibilité des minéraux in vitro - Évaluer la biodisponibilité minérale in vitro - Effectuer des essais cliniques liés à la nutrition humaine enrichie en nouvelles sources minérales (clé) - Soutenir les activités d'enseignement et co-superviser les étudiants en maîtrise et en baccalauréat - Agir à l'interface entre la science et la technologie lors de la supervision des étudiants et de la collaboration avec des partenaires du milieu universitaire et de l'industrie - Demandes de subvention d ' appui à l ' équipe et activités connexes du Centre Singapour-ETH, Centre Bezos

jobs.description:
Doctoral Researcher in Food Processing for Planetary and Human Health

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

The ETH Sustainable Food Processing Group focuses on advancing food processing technologies and their role in sustainable food systems, using innovative approaches to tackle fundamental challenges such as the protein transition and food security. We use innovative sustainability assessment and emerging food system approaches as key tools to guide processing innovations toward holistic and impactful solutions.

Job description

We are looking for a:

• Highly motivated candidate to join a collaborative research project that explores how food processing affects both nutritional quality and environmental impact.

The overall vision is to identify and develop processing strategies that improve nutritional quality and environmental performance as assessed by nutritional life cycle assessment (nLCA) while creating appealing hybrid protein-rich products. Thus, in addition to executing processing trials, the role includes coordinating collaborations within the team and with external partners to ensure that nutritional, health, and sustainability aspects are systematically integrated into the research.

Our two well-equipped pilot plants, featuring technologies ranging from multi-scale extruders to high-pressure and thermal treatment systems, pulsed electric field (PEF) equipment, and more, will serve as the core experimental platform for the project. Advanced analytical methods (e.g., nutritional profile, bioaccessibility, dynamic mechanical analysis, imaging, spectroscopy) may be employed to assess product quality.

Profile

The candidate must hold a:

• Master’s degree (or equivalent) in Food Technology, Food Engineering, Food Science, Bioengineering, Biotechnology or a closely related field.

In addition, the candidate should have:

• Excellent academic qualifications.

• Advanced knowledge in food processing.

• Strong communication and writing skills and high self-motivation.

• Openness to interdisciplinary work and a flexible mindset.

• Enthusiasm for engineering, food technology, and sustainability-related questions.

• Expertise in structurization via extrusion, disintegration, or preservation technologies, as well as project management and nutrition, will be considered a plus.

Workplace

Workplace

We offer

• A multicultural group with a diverse and interdisciplinary team composition.

• Exciting and varied projects in an innovative environment.

• Personal development opportunities through training, teaching, and further education.

• Perspectives for career development.

• A dynamic, collegial working environment with flat hierarchies.

chevron_right
Working, teaching and research at ETH Zurich

We value diversity and sustainability

In line with our values , ETH Zurich encourages an inclusive culture. We promote equality of opportunity, value diversity and nurture a working and learning environment in which the rights and dignity of all our staff and students are respected. Visit our Equal Opportunities and Diversity website to find out how we ensure a fair and open environment that allows everyone to grow and flourish. Sustainability is a core value for us – we are consistently working towards a climate-neutral future .

Curious? So are we.

We look forward to receiving your online application (English, PDF format), including:

• Motivation letter (max. 1 page) outlining your qualifications and motivation for this project.

• Research proposal (max. 3 pages) on "Future of food processing for affordable, nutritious and more sustainable foods", addressing current challenges, key literature, and innovative approaches.

• CV with list of scientific outputs (e.g., theses, papers).

• Contact details of 2 referees.

• Copies of BSc and MSc diplomas*.

• Copies of BSc and MSc theses (any language)*.

• Transcript listing exams with ECTS credits and grades.

• 1 recommendation letter.
